papers.title: The RSI Tax: When Recursive Self-Improvement Is Not Worth the Cost
papers.code_note: Complete nineteen-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–D, four figures, nine tables, accounting equations and note prompt read on 2026-11-13; main figures and detailed cost tables visually inspected. An official implementation or complete run-log release was not independently verified. No research code, agents, benchmarks or models executed.
papers.learning_signal: Completed-task trajectories and scalar verifier outcomes guide note, skill or harness updates around frozen backbones; ReasoningBank uses its separate internal trajectory judge.
papers.mechanism: Scores each arriving task before its feedback can update retained state, and separates task-execution tokens from verification, exploration and writing tokens. A bounded-note baseline revises up to 2,048 tokens from failed-task excerpts every four tasks without candidate search. State resets between repository chains; terminal tasks retain it across one ordered stream.
papers.evaluation: Complete v1 compares six methods and two backbones on seven selected fifteen-task repository chains and 89 terminal tasks. The note baseline matches or exceeds the observed accuracy of three search-heavy methods in all four settings, with 65.6–71.0% mean within-setting token savings. Verification contributes 74.8–93.6% of their pooled update tokens.
papers.limitations: Fixed streams and no independent-run uncertainty limit comparative generalization. Meta-Harness uses an adapted strict-improvement selector and EvoSkill refreshes a rolling frontier, so some overhead reflects these implementations. Feedback use also differs. Tokens, including cached input, are not dollars or FLOPs. Subsequent use is not causal benefit, and finite-horizon non-use does not prove removable waste; the study does not test a learned cost-aware update policy.

papers.title: Correct Answers from Insufficient Histories: A Controlled Study of Agent Memory Evaluation
papers.code_note: Complete fourteen-page v1 and Appendices A–F read on 2026-11-12; certificate definitions and main result tables visually inspected. Authors retain code and receipts but state that the artifact is not publicly released. No research code or models executed.
papers.learning_signal: No agent-learning method is proposed; masking, packing, event replay and same-context counterexamples supply evaluation labels.
papers.mechanism: Separates hidden-reference agreement from evidence sufficiency and appropriate answering. Legal histories with identical visible bytes but different answers certify insufficiency; public chronological/cutoff rules certify some sufficient prefixes. Unclassified cases remain separate.
papers.evaluation: Two hosted readers each receive 1,600 requests over the same eighty confirmation histories. On 203 insufficient raw-prefix cases, Qwen and DeepSeek match 87 and 85 hidden references but appropriately abstain only seven and twenty-one times. A separate 120-history judge audit reports 99.38% accuracy yet retains support errors; a deterministic baseline matches the hybrid’s perfect constructed-case score.
papers.limitations: Short synthetic logs and fixed queries do not establish natural-domain prevalence or lifelong-memory gains. Replication reuses exposed histories and Qwen-tokenized inputs. Certified-subset intervals leave CSV improvements inconclusive, not equivalent. Programs share certifier rules; no human adjudication or public artifact independently validates them. Abstention is a declared contract, not every application’s optimal policy.

papers.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
papers.learning_signal: Training/validation task feedback and archived traces drive harness edits; post-hoc diagnostics inform fixed evolution-operator revisions.
papers.mechanism: Audits frozen evolved harnesses for repeated success, gained/lost task coverage, component interactions and candidate retention. EvoAudit uses those diagnostics to revise four operators; AGE installs the fixed revisions into A-Evolve, retaining fixed models, evaluator contracts and editing boundaries.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 studies four adapted recipes with two harnesses on banking and terminal tasks, eight execution passes, external transfer, common-process parent expansion, selected component interventions and frozen-pool gate replay. AGE adds four 20-generation runs and eight-expert review of proposed operator revisions.
papers.limitations: Each configuration has one evolution lineage, not eight independent searches; headline source-benchmark scores include training and validation tasks. Parent and gate diagnostics use selected frozen pools, and component cases favor separable changes. AGE bundles revisions informed by the studied settings without individual operator ablations or external AGE transfer. Diagnostic/design costs are separate from online evolution; gains still coexist with regressions.

papers.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
papers.learning_signal: Automatic validation scores, prior code edits and execution traces; a supplied component library supports proposals.
papers.mechanism: A fixed coding agent proposes complete executable harness edits using an optional component library. Tree-based selection mixes validation score and direct-child exploration; compatible candidates enter the archive even when they score worse. The chosen harness persists with a frozen executor, while the outer search procedure stays fixed.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 evaluates fifteen candidate attempts plus the root on six agent, coding and web benchmarks, with disjoint validation/test tasks and five executions per task. It reports component/exploration controls, cumulative edit lineages, execution costs and three benchmarks optimized again with a stronger executor.
papers.limitations: Five execution repeats do not establish variability across independent searches. A stronger model proposes edits, and equal candidate counts do not equal total compute. Execution costs exclude search and are not uniformly lowest; WebShop reports a continuous score. Stronger-executor experiments rerun optimization rather than transfer a frozen harness, and lineage improvements do not isolate individual edits.

papers.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: All substantive text, seven figures, the results table, equations and references of the 15-page arXiv v2 read on 2026-11-09; no appendix is included. Official training implementation and a complete reproduction configuration were not established. Referenced distillation kernels are separate software, and no code or training was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Coding rewards, auxiliary criterion rewards and designed textual hints on failing agent turns.
papers.mechanism: Combines GRPO coding/criterion rewards with full-vocabulary reverse-KL distillation at failing turns. The teacher shares current policy weights but receives a designed local hint and is stop-gradient within each update. Reasoning and response tokens receive the auxiliary signal; its contribution vanishes when all criteria pass.
papers.evaluation: Complete v2 studies a new semantic-search argument, seven final-response style criteria and interleaved poem-status requirements using a harness-adapted Qwen3-Coder-30B. It compares representative RL/distillation variants, failing-turn versus always-on guidance, distillation weights and reasoning-token inclusion.
papers.limitations: The feedback strings, criteria and procedure are supplied. Evidence concerns style/tool formatting in one coding setup; broad held-out transfer is not established. Table deviations summarize the last 32 training steps, not independent runs, and equal mean coding scores are not a non-inferiority guarantee. High distillation weights can collapse performance. Conditional improvement heuristics and disappearing auxiliary loss do not establish general convergence.

papers.title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
papers.venue: Author reports NeurIPS 2026 PALM workshop; primary venue record not verified.
papers.code_note: Complete 18-page arXiv v1, Appendix A.1–A.15, three figures/fifteen tables and objective read on 2026-11-09. The workshop website had no paper-specific program and its public venue API was restricted, so acceptance remains author-reported. Official implementation availability was not established; no training or research code was run.
papers.learning_signal: Memory-derived synthetic questions and a frozen base-model teacher conditioned on recent memory guide per-user adapter updates.
papers.mechanism: A persistent per-user LoRA adapter learns from student-sampled answers scored by a frozen base-model teacher given recent extracted memory. The hybrid always retrieves query- and answer-based evidence, verifies the adapter answer, then uses the adapter-free model to regenerate unsupported or conflicting answers from the merged text store.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 reports 1,438 native HaluMem questions from eight users, delayed re-asks, a 1,586-question LoCoMo comparison, model-scale tests, earlier recipe probes and routing/cost diagnostics. Native-question and pooled-age results are distinct; user-clustered intervals do not measure training-run variability.
papers.limitations: Recent-memory gains diminish with age. Routing lowers HaluMem conflict accuracy; on LoCoMo its overall gain comes with lower scores on all four answerable categories and much higher abstention accuracy. Some appendix probes use different recipes, and reported rubric errors are author diagnoses. Training compute is omitted from cost totals; token savings do not establish lower GPU cost or a validated break-even point.

papers.title: Towards Robust Long-Lived Agents: Benchmarking Experience Lifecycles in Evolving Environments
papers.code_note: All substantive main text, Appendices A–D, metric formulas, fourteen figures, six tables and full case records of the 29-page arXiv v1 read on 2026-11-09. Official README at 4780ba6 documents the framework and separate case assets, Python/Docker requirements and an ARM64 setup. No assets were downloaded or research software installed/executed.
papers.learning_signal: Tool observations and permitted later outcome feedback; private reference inventories are used only for scoring.
papers.mechanism: Pairs streams retaining versus clearing memory, skills and history under a fixed Hermes framework and model. Silent changes invalidate selected environment knowledge. Post-task reference-based judging tracks saved knowledge separately from programmatic task outcomes; background skill review can revise experience before grading.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 evaluates twenty models, 352 tasks, eighteen simulated applications and twenty-six changes. It adds two-judge agreement checks, task-matched request analyses, selective-update cohorts, exposure and persistence follow-ups, and foreground action accounting.
papers.limitations: One stream per model/environment/condition does not measure repeat variability, and action-induced states diverge. Knowledge coverage is not precision; first-completion recovery is not sustained correctness, and post-change performance is not a before/after delta. Correlations and selected trace cohorts do not establish causality. Foreground counts exclude background computation, and judge agreement does not establish independent accuracy.

papers.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
papers.code_note: Author project page inspected on 2026-11-09 and explicitly labels code as coming soon. The full paper includes prompts, algorithms and learned Meta-Skills, but no released implementation or independent execution was established.
papers.learning_signal: Training-only terminal verifier outcomes and privileged verifier-informed rollouts supply act, avoid and hold contrasts. Fixed reflection, aggregation and update prompts turn them into reusable guidance; online decisions use the active trace and permitted workspace evidence.
papers.mechanism: Learns a textual Meta-Skill offline, then freezes it to guide a separate evolver at checkpoints within each task. Bounded notices, instructions, hooks and tools alter the ongoing run without resetting its environment. Harness edits are discarded between runs; the model and offline learning procedure stay fixed.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v1 tests 60 held-out Terminal-Bench tasks with five repetitions and 75 DeepSWE tasks with three. It reports repetition-level variation, component/reset and checkpoint ablations, and separate construction/deployment costs. A second backbone uses a separately learned Meta-Skill.
papers.limitations: Independent rollout contrasts do not identify an edit’s causal effect; the appendix also discloses worker-prompt and segmentation differences in no-evolver comparisons. Repeated evaluation does not measure variation in rebuilding the Meta-Skill. Costs depend on reuse volume, and code, audit effectiveness and broader transfer remain unverified.

papers.title: From AutoResearch to Continual AutoResearch: Do Agents Learn Across Tasks?
papers.code_note: Complete 27-page arXiv v1, substantive Appendices A–D, seventeen figures/thirteen tables, generator and metric definitions, and all trace cases read on 2026-11-09. The manuscript promises code with camera-ready publication; an official runnable release and complete run configuration were not established. No research agents or experiments were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Visible development data and execution feedback guide research; hidden test scores are computed afterward.
papers.mechanism: Compares retained native sessions, files and experimental state with reset instances of the same fixed agent. Hidden evaluation separates first-valid quality, time-integrated best-candidate quality and final selection. Fresh-session matched/shuffled insight cards test explicit knowledge transfer separately from continuous sessions.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 covers five CLI agents, nine task families and 32 transfer tasks per agent, mostly with 30-minute budgets. It reports candidate-count and initialization controls, budget/stream-length probes, a four-agent Energy-stream memory ablation and selected trace cases. Aggregate early-search gains coexist with mixed final outcomes.
papers.limitations: Four agents have one matched run pair; one has three repeats. Native harnesses confound cross-model comparisons. Search utility combines timing with normalized hidden quality and does not establish equal compute or monetary savings. Adjusted controls change the measured quantity, and later-candidate cohorts shrink. Short fixed streams, limited memory probes and disclosed host contention do not establish broad continual scientific improvement.

papers.title: Can Benign Skills Induce Misaligned Behavior in LLM Agents?
papers.code_note: Complete 12-page arXiv v1, Appendix A.1–A.6, five figures/six tables, skill examples and judging/guard protocols read on 2026-11-09. An official runnable artifact and complete per-condition judgment coverage were not established. No attacks, model runs or research code were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Successful benign traces and benign validation feedback build and refine skills; harmful-task outcomes are reserved for evaluation.
papers.mechanism: Retrieves benign procedural skills for fixed-model agents, then measures executed safety violations separately from harmful-objective completion. A fixed editor also evolves skill banks using benign validation alone. Retrieval, exact content removal, source-trajectory comparisons and a terminating pre-execution guard probe the resulting behavior.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 covers five backbones on AgentHarm, LPS-Bench and SafeAgentBench, with 316 benign/harmful task pairs and disjoint construction requests. It compares trajectory-derived, expert and mixed banks, 100-step evolution, and narrower Qwen3 content/guard analyses.
papers.limitations: Harmful requests are supplied; this does not measure spontaneous misconduct during benign use. Unresolved trajectories without identified violations are excluded from unsafe-action denominators, and independent-run uncertainty is not reported. Content interventions jointly alter wording, length and information. The guard terminates blocked/error runs without replanning, costs benign utility and leaves residual violations; its evidence does not cover all five backbones.

papers.title: Artifact-to-Capability: Diagnosing Breaks in Capability Formation of Self-Evolving Agents in a Controlled Environment
papers.code_note: All substantive text, Appendices A–G, five figures/eleven tables, formal criteria, board traces and code excerpts of the 19-page arXiv v1 read on 2026-11-09. An official runnable artifact was not established. No game, model or research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Game outcomes and traces drive the evaluated evolvers; independent game rules diagnose retained artifacts.
papers.mechanism: Proposes a five-property diagnostic for converting persistent artifacts into useful behavior. Frozen-system interventions compare identical board states, complete games and successive code versions, separating legal moves, useful legal choices, composition failures and later retention.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 studies Gomoku adaptations of Reflexion, Voyager and DGM with one shared backbone, 120 constructed/transformed states, 1,756 evolution-derived states, twenty seeded games per tested configuration and a 7,234-state late-version comparison. It includes component removals, paired transition tables and score decomposition.
papers.limitations: The proposed definition excludes legality-only gains; it is not a universal definition of learning. These adaptations are not original-system replications, and diagnostic states largely come from DGM evolution. Reflexion has one sample per state/condition and only one control rerun. Game seeds are not independent evolution runs; local-state improvement need not beat the initial strategy at complete games. Generalization and failure prevalence remain untested.

papers.title: A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory
papers.learning_signal: New evidence, scoped state conflicts and model judgments of dependency strength and alternative support.
papers.mechanism: Stores scoped, versioned states and proposes directed support dependencies from history. The same frozen LLM tests whether a dependent claim survives removal of a premise. Strict dependencies propagate revisions only when no independent current support survives; weak dependencies trigger uncertainty handling without recursive propagation.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 reports direct revision, dependency recovery and cascade invalidation on 50 constructed StateChangeBench cases with one backbone, including verification/support/propagation ablations and ported cascade mechanisms. It also gives point estimates on six public memory benchmarks; impact-set F1, edge F1 and closure consistency have different targets and denominators.
papers.limitations: Run counts and the double-annotated subset size were not retained; action-decision and premise-gate results were omitted because aggregation could not be reconstructed. Small depth strata lack uncertainty tests. The same model proposes, verifies and assesses support, so closure consistency is not independent correctness. Public-benchmark scores are mixed and do not establish non-degradation or deployed action safety.

papers.title: Can Coding Agents Sustain Continual Evolution without Forgetting?
papers.code_note: All substantive text, Appendices A–B, five figures/two tables and code examples of the 14-page arXiv v1 read on 2026-11-09. README and evaluation lock at bb84e4a inspected: the current artifact specifies 30-minute rollouts/250 steps and a one-hour sandbox lifetime, distinct from the main text’s one-hour execution wording. No installation or execution; historical runtime equivalence unverified.
papers.learning_signal: Task execution traces and benchmark outcomes drive harness edits; prior-task reevaluation measures retention.
papers.mechanism: Sequentially edits Mini-SWE-Agent prompts, control flow and tools with a fixed backbone using adapted AHE and Meta-Harness. Re-evaluation of source tasks measures retention after changing task type; selected edit interventions investigate incompatible verification gates, workflows and time-budget policies.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 examines six two-stage directions among 50 SWE-bench Verified, 50 paraphrased SWT-Bench and 30 FeatureBench tasks, with two rollouts per task/round. It analyzes 520 trajectories and representative edit bundles, plus a prompt-template routing case.
papers.limitations: Optimization and reporting reuse the sampled subsets; no disjoint held-out evaluation or independent-search uncertainty is described. Scores are not full-benchmark results. Some losses follow mechanically incompatible artifact gates, not erased model knowledge. Selected edit bundles and pairwise transitions do not establish universal conflict prevalence or inevitable forgetting in longer sequences.

papers.title: Evolving Memory, Learning to Meta-Control: Test-Time Adaptation for Experience-augmented LLM Agents
papers.code_note: All substantive main text, Appendices A–J, five figures/six tables, full regret derivation, algorithm, configuration and cases of the 22-page arXiv v1 read on 2026-11-09. Official method implementation availability was not established; linked benchmark repositories are separate artifacts. No code, model or benchmark was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task outcomes update linear bandit estimates; trajectories and feedback drive language-model memory revisions.
papers.mechanism: A four-action contextual bandit selects direct solving, episodic reuse, guidance reuse or pre-solve distillation from numeric retrieval features. External memories and small linear routing models persist; the backbone and learning procedure stay fixed. Optional retries inject failure insights, with the pseudocode crediting the final attempt reward to the original routing decision.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 compares four backbones on 1,140 BigCodeBench, 500 SWE-bench Verified, 273 MultiChallenge and 1,200 selected BBEH instances. It separates first-attempt and four-attempt success, reports fixed/heuristic routing and controller-freezing controls, and analyzes tokens and a restricted stationary-bandit model.
papers.limitations: One run per configuration; 100 BigCodeBench tuning tasks remain in evaluation. First-attempt gains do not imply better four-attempt success, and some fixed or memory-free baselines win. Shared-snapshot chronology and a separate learned-policy snapshot score are unclear. Token totals exclude evaluator calls. The stationary, undiscounted theoretical controller differs from the discounted experimental variants and does not guarantee optimal long-term memory consolidation.

papers.title: Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement
papers.code_note: Complete 20-page arXiv v1, substantive Appendices A–C, eight figures/eight tables, algorithm, formulation, construction/judging protocols and robustness checks read on 2026-11-09. The author publication page lists a preprint; an official implementation was not established. No skill, model or benchmark was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Incoming skill bodies, similar earlier skills, and body-derived synthetic queries guide metadata rewriting without evaluation labels.
papers.mechanism: Refines an incoming skill’s name and description using its body and similar earlier skills, adding differentiating capabilities, scope exclusions and name qualifiers. Original records supply later references. Rewritten metadata persists while skill bodies, earlier metadata and router weights remain fixed; fidelity is prompted rather than formally verified.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 evaluates a deliberately confusable SRA-Bench growth stream across five routers, two additional benchmark streams, random additions, component combinations and limited order/repeat controls. Native Codex tests score named-skill selection; a separate 150-query, 87-skill experiment reports hidden-test task success.
papers.limitations: Main routing metrics count annotated required skills, not execution success. Required-skill metadata stays original while confusable incoming skills are refined; construction and error typing use model judgments. Random additions yield smaller gains. Query-bootstrap intervals do not capture all rewrite/order variability. Task-success evidence uses an early library and extra workflow instruction, with much smaller gains than skill-selection coverage.

papers.title: Learning to Live: A Step Toward Lifelong Embodied Intelligence
papers.code_note: Complete 39-page arXiv v2, Appendices A–D, thirteen figures/eighteen tables and official component documentation read on 2026-11-09. The formerly unavailable repository is now accessible: RoboBeats inference and SSS benchmark/evaluation components were inspected at a63e763c515136a5090f9fb251f7b72f702ad93a. This is not a verified complete robot-memory/EDM release or reproduction. Code is Apache-2.0; benchmark questions/rubrics have a separate CC BY-NC 4.0 license. Nothing installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Temporal labels train perception adapters; selected observations, task difficulty, and execution feedback support memory and tool construction.
papers.mechanism: Combines an offline-trained causal perception gate, a revisitable store of visual observations and ReSight’s Explore–Distill–Mount procedure for reusable tools and skills. RoboBeats changes LoRA parameters during training; runtime adaptation changes retained evidence, derived indexes and programs. The gate’s small model is part of a larger writer/reader pipeline.
papers.evaluation: Full v2 evaluates streaming perception, selective memory writing and a reconstructed 24-hour robot recording with six questions repeated three times. ReSight supplies the capability-expansion experiments, including separate held-out episodes. Matched-condition gains coexist with protocol-sensitive comparisons and accuracy–cost tradeoffs.
papers.limitations: The integrated experiment is offline replay of one day, without actions changing future observations. Partial-credit answer scores are not physical task success; input and turn protocols differ across configurations. ReSight results are reused evidence, and online token savings exclude construction and training. Some gating/review settings reduce accuracy; writer, reader and judge dependence limits attribution. Retention exemptions mean the nominal per-view budget is not a global storage bound.

papers.title: Exo: An Architecture for Self-Improving Systems at Runtime
papers.code_note: Complete 14-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–B, seven figures/two tables, preservation proof and measurement rules read on 2026-11-09. Paper-pinned README c5c1963 and current official docs inspected; current docs identify the earlier self-evolution experiment separately from the hosting runtime. The pinned artifact link is retained; no installation, game or benchmark execution.
papers.learning_signal: Execution history, model cost, failures, and task feedback inform runtime code and policy revisions.
papers.mechanism: Makes the running harness executor editable, including tools, context construction and the procedures for further revision. A separate mechanism is intended to preserve history/artifact versions and govern activation. Learned code persists within ongoing work and into later tasks while model weights remain unchanged.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 compares game objectives with Codex/Pi, then compares editing enabled/disabled from the same starting policy on AppWorld, SREGym and nineteen CLB coding issues. It reports within-run specialization, retained-state transfer, three AppWorld seeds, five coding runs and a negative low-reuse quest condition.
papers.limitations: The preservation argument assumes enforced mediation outside the editable policy; the broadly writable development setup does not satisfy that boundary. Build-only acceptance guarantees neither correctness nor recovery. Game objectives have one standalone/transfer pair each; graded transfer stays within scenarios or fault families, and coding has no holdout. Reported cost is model usage, and SREGym correctness is described without detailed rates. Recursive improvement of the improvement strategy is enabled, not separately quantified.

papers.title: Is It the Curriculum or Just the Easy Start? Benchmarking Unsupervised Environment Design on Quadrupeds
papers.code_note: Complete 22-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–F, ten figures/twelve tables, metrics and terrain equations read on 2026-11-09. Official README, MIT license and dependency manifest inspected at 56036e5bc22ab6c961701925dab8a83bb6367869. Documented reproduction requires external/generated assets and GPU training; ONNX export support is not physical-robot validation. No installation, simulation or training executed.
papers.learning_signal: Student rewards and curriculum-specific regret, learning-progress, replay, or terrain-difficulty rules.
papers.mechanism: Compares fourteen terrain-selection curricula around a shared PPO training design. Methods change randomization difficulty, replay buffers, mutated levels or a learned generator using success, value-loss, learning-progress or regret signals. Five robot-specific policies learn persistent weights; the curriculum algorithms themselves remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 reports 350 training runs: fourteen methods, five simulated quadrupeds and five seeds. Final policies face random and held-out structured terrain, cross-fitted tail evaluation and feature envelopes. Easy/mixed randomization is competitive on several random-level sets, while held-out leaders differ on three robots.
papers.limitations: One PPO design and finite robot-specific budgets do not establish universal curriculum rankings or physical-robot transfer. Nominal environment-step matching excludes PAIRED antagonist work and includes non-training replay-scoring steps. SFL and robotics methods are adapted variants. Uncorrected five-seed tests define top groups by failure to reject a gap, not equivalence; high variance can enlarge those groups. Terrain ranges and success constraints are not equally difficult across robots.

papers.title: Long-Term Agent Memory through Complementary Curation and Consolidation
papers.code_note: Complete nine-page final paper and Appendices A–E read on 2026-11-11; key result tables and retrieval plot visually inspected. Official implementation not independently verified. No research code executed.
papers.learning_signal: Conversation transcripts and timestamps drive model-generated episode/tuple extraction and offline merge/delete decisions; model weights stay fixed.
papers.mechanism: Stores session-level episodes beside timestamped relational tuples with source context. UMAP/HDBSCAN clusters memories for LLM consolidation. Separate semantic retrieval supplies ten episodes and twenty tuples; the tuple store does not perform graph traversal.
papers.evaluation: Final paper reports LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S QA, memory-component ablations, four backbones and retrieval/clustering sweeps. GPT-4.1-mini scores 90.2% on LoCoMo versus 91.3% full context and 85.5% on LongMemEval-S. Consolidation reduces memory items by about 16.3% while lowering LoCoMo score by one point.
papers.limitations: Several baseline scores are imported from prior work, and repeated-run uncertainty is unreported. QA on stored dialogues does not demonstrate online task learning or lifelong retention. Preference questions regress relative to Nemori; compression is not total compute or latency savings. Missing consolidation-prompt and noise-point handling details limit reconstruction.

papers.title: MUSE: Multi-Level Memory with Selective Runtime Injection for Scientific Coding Agents
papers.code_note: Complete 17-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–B, eight figures/six tables, retrieval equations and all prompt templates read on 2026-11-09. Official README and root inventory inspected at 524ddcd70fa5412e24601fa69d367fab2838170c. papers.learning_signal: Historical task requirements, trajectories, submissions, and success/failure feedback support lesson extraction and review.
papers.mechanism: Extracts approach and implementation lessons, including conditional explanations of failures, then consolidates global guidance offline. Frozen global and Top5 approach memories initialize new tasks. Four runtime retrieval routes produce at most four source records; a fixed LLM gate injects one with generated review advice or abstains. Model weights, tools and the tested bank remain fixed.

The gate control changes selection, advice and extra model computation together. Random problem splits and related-kernel transfer do not establish broader domain transfer. papers.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
papers.code_note: Complete 32-page arXiv v2, Appendices A–F, eleven figures/fourteen tables, all proofs and thirty-three equations read on 2026-11-09. Official README inspected at c91d859c21f38f10e358091265eea6e571e23e47, including separate controlled/coding experiments and external model, container and teacher-service requirements. No code, model or environment installed or run.
papers.learning_signal: Task rewards support controlled policy training; sampled actions and stronger-teacher probes estimate deployment mismatch.
papers.mechanism: Under a finite KL-regularized semantic-control model, expresses return as an interface-specific optimum minus policy mismatch and separates target shift, training residual and changed model readout. Controlled adapter training tests interface-specific preferences; action sampling estimates mismatch, with a teacher substituted for the unavailable coding-agent optimum.
papers.evaluation: Full v2 combines exact evaluation on compiled graphs for three MiniWoB++ families and six harnesses, nine selected adaptation swaps, presentation controls and estimator calibration. A separate five-harness study reports three runs on 39 Terminal-Bench Lite tasks, with teacher-based diagnostics on three probe tasks.
papers.limitations: The exact ceiling depends on the reference and regularized objective, not just raw success or physical capability. Task-bootstrap intervals do not establish training-seed robustness. Adaptation prediction uses already-trained target checkpoints and oracle quantities; accurate sampled diagnostics require large query budgets. Coding estimates use coarse action categories, incomplete probe cohorts and a nonoptimal teacher, so five-harness rank agreement is not a certified regret bound or general selector.

Paired comparisons examine retention, recovery, instructions, revision scope, feedback and commit validation; finite controls, longitudinal cases and a MemOps audit add complementary evidence.
papers.limitations: Benchmarks use one writer, fixed budgets and one draw per cell, with queries clustered by history or persona. LoCoMo rankings depend on task composition and scoring conventions. Two-event revision studies use deterministic rules; guarantees require complete dependencies and sound checks. Carryover and validation benefits vary by reader, and natural-language checking remains unvalidated.

papers.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning

papers.learning_signal: Environment rewards train slow parameters with PPO; self-supervised prediction updates fast neural-memory parameters during interaction.
papers.mechanism: Meta-trains a policy, neural-memory initialization and update machinery with PPO. Within each episode, causal self-supervised gradient updates change temporary fast weights; final representations become summaries available to later episodes of the same trial. Slow parameters freeze at meta-test, fast weights reset each episode, and summary history resets for each new trial.

ML10/ML45 reveal goals, and PointMaze holds out start/goal pairs rather than maze layouts. Default aggregation costs O(E²T) over E episodes of horizon T; only the EMA variant is O(ET). TTT is slower at short contexts. Cost/representation plots are implementation-specific or descriptive, and unreleased code prevents verification of exact baseline integration and reproduction.

papers.title: Recursive Self-Improvement on a Budget: Scoring Code Edits Before They Run

papers.title: Auditing the Product, Not the Recursion: The Evaluation Evidence Behind Recursive Self-Improvement Claims
papers.code_note: Complete 39-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–D, twenty tables, figure, all three proofs, codebook revisions, query log, 114-study table and twenty-anchor comparison read on 2026-11-09. papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: a study of reported evaluation designs.
papers.mechanism: Measures reported evaluation designs against distinct claims about final products, accumulation, repeatability and improvement of the improver. papers.title: Are Self-Evolving Agents Continual Learners?
papers.code_note: Complete 24-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–E, nine figures/five tables, eleven equations, retrieval details and all seed/environment prompts read on 2026-11-09. Prompt shares and similarity averages are diagnostic associations, not causal attribution or proof that every threshold fails. papers.title: REM: What to Store, When to Recall, What to Forget in Experience Memory for Coding Agents
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2026 CLEA Workshop — accepted poster (workshop, not main conference)
papers.code_note: Complete 16-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–G, three figures/fourteen tables, algorithm, injection mechanics and schema/accounting details read on 2026-11-09. papers.learning_signal: Completed trajectories supply structured experience; a hand-written in-loop struggle signal controls when detailed records enter context.
papers.mechanism: Consolidates a fixed pool of solved coding traces into short localize/understand/fix/verify documents. A retrieved document persists throughout the new task; a handwritten first-failed-validation trigger exposes a detailed record for one turn only. The record is then removed, while the agent’s own response remains in history. The evaluated pool does not grow online.

Retrieval baselines use their own published configurations; the discovered-schema pool is incomplete after API failures. Identifier mentions do not prove causal use. Stronger recipients can be harmed, record eviction is incomplete forgetting, and text-to-SQL schema generation is not a second-domain task-success evaluation.

papers.title: RIFAR: Reliability-Informed and Forgetting-Aware Replay for Continual Robot Learning with World-Action Models
papers.learning_signal: New-task demonstrations, inverse-dynamics consistency of generated replay and action-prediction drift after adaptation.
papers.mechanism: Retains short real demonstration prefixes and generates historical replay with a world-action model. A trainable inverse-dynamics model screens action–visual consistency. After initial adaptation, a second phase prioritizes reliable replay whose action predictions changed most. Both policy and reliability model update; generated replay is discarded between stages while historical prefixes persist.

Goal AUC is 90.97 under the paper’s group/checkpoint weighting, using 320 historical steps per task. Real experiments use demonstrations, manual resets and manual outcome judgments.

Reliability screening still admits failed trajectories; small pools can duplicate samples. AUC is not final retention, and its initial six-task group receives the same weight as each new task. Fixed orders, absent confidence intervals and extra generation/model-training costs limit broader claims. Stored-step savings exclude total memory and compute.

papers.title: Self-Evolving Defense: Continual Security Policy Learning for LLM Agents

Later episodes retrieve specific rules and covering parents into context. Memory stays read-only during an episode; DTap additionally uses per-turn policy injection and a pre-tool guard.

papers.title: Context Language Models
papers.code_note: Complete available 27-page arXiv v1, main sections and Appendices A-G, read on 2026-11-13; all 22 figures and five tables visually checked. papers.title: SAGE: A Statistical Acceptance Gate for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Complete 10-page arXiv v1, both figures, both tables and equations 1–11 read on 2026-11-10; figures and tables visually checked. It accepts only when paired wins exceed asymmetrically penalized regressions, an exact conditional binomial test rejects the break-even null, and an empirical regression cap holds. Actor weights and the SkillOpt proposal mechanism remain fixed.

It tests paired candidate–incumbent outcomes and allocates error across rounds, candidates and possible decision histories. Under independent IID evaluation and strict feedback isolation, promotions and a private cumulative progress certificate have simultaneous statistical validity.

Holdout-estimated improvement is not known population truth. Main search also uses development drafts/prescreening absent from comparators, and named baselines are adapted styles. Lower bounds concern a restricted threshold class; near-equal mean gains do not establish equivalence or transfer to coding and safety metrics.

Most reported training uses one seed, and math scores also inform hyperparameter search. Baseline and distillation controls differ in supervision detail and compute. Main text specifies forward KL while appendix main-configuration labels specify generalized JSD; FIDE and win-rate aggregation is also unreconciled. Correlations with search agreement do not establish internal algorithm transfer.

papers.title: LifeMem: Enabling Lifelong Experience Reuse for LLM Agents

papers.title: Safety in Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
papers.code_note: Author-linked survey repository and project page inspected on 2026-11-09. This artifact is a coded literature collection, not a reproduced agent defense; its corpus labels and surveyed experiments were not independently rerun.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable to the survey itself; it analyzes selection signals, authorization conditions and feedback that govern reusable agent-state updates.
papers.mechanism: SAVER follows a substrate–adaptation transition through violation, exposure and response, distinguishing local utility from permission for broader reuse. It separates storage from activation, propagation from migration, and immediate containment from repair of derived memories, skills, artifacts or model state.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v1 synthesizes a scoping corpus with explicit source, deduplication and coding rules. Its benchmark tables compare observed lifecycle stages and paper-specific denominators; proposed measures cover safe promotion, boundary change, negative evidence and reactivation after repair and resumed adaptation.
papers.limitations: The 683-record inventory is not 683 independently appraised safety demonstrations: 549 classifications remain low-confidence. Screening lacks independent dual coding or preregistration, and heterogeneous results are not pooled. Proposed metrics and the conceptual authority model do not certify safety, complete recovery or the prevalence of benign adaptation drift.

papers.title: Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses

papers.title: MASkills: Continual Skills Optimization for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

papers.title: Memory Anchors for Continual Robot Learning

A reserved share of replay contains these anchors, with the remainder sampled for diversity.

High-conflict pairs are selected from baseline outcomes; task/permutation observations are not independent training replicates. Enrichment trades diversity for specificity and does not help every suite. Real tasks are short, curated and demonstration-driven. The printed AUC normalization is inconsistent with its stated range; implementation details remain unverified.

papers.title: Coalition-Aware Skill Reliability for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.learning_signal: Source outcome rewards and sampled skill-coalition knockout scores; unlabeled target-query retrieval similarity guides transfer masking.

CASS ranks candidate banks using sampled, size-normalized coalition-removal margins plus outcome reward, rather than computing every skill’s Shapley value. After transfer, u-SMCO greedily masks skills whose removal improves a cosine-retrieval proxy on unlabeled target queries and contexts; the retained bank persists for later inference.

Source-positive insert has a negative target point estimate, but its target confidence interval includes zero.

Exact positive bank gain identifies the new skill’s full-bank marginal, while other contributions remain unidentified. Retrieval similarity is a proxy; target data are required, probe/evaluation separation is unspecified, and small point improvements and step costs do not establish uniform superiority.

papers.title: CIDER: Continual Interactive Distillation for Embodied Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Complete twenty-page v1, Appendices A–F, ten figures, eleven tables, all loss definitions and Algorithm 1 read on 2026-11-10; figures/tables and baseline equations visually checked. papers.title: EvolveNet: Collaborative Harness Evolution for Agent Self-Improvement

papers.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents

Synthetic isolated families and benchmark-driven runtime design limit ecological and unseen-family generalization. Transfer is mixed, procedural performance can regress, and Hermes+ uses about 2.5 times the tokens. Native adapters, budgets and release instructions require configuration reconciliation.

papers.title: GDPevo: Evaluating Agent Self-Evolution on Real Business Tasks
papers.code_note: Complete 22-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–H, five figures, six tables and all four diagnostic cases read on 2026-11-10. Official Apache-2.0 repository snapshot 5082a777379156a048881e94940d640702e5e09a documents construction/evaluation workspaces and released results. Frozen-model agents distill permitted demonstrations, environment exploration or three rounds of score feedback into persistent skills, which fresh agents load for held-out work.

Deterministic graders do not establish expert semantic validity, and group-level standard deviations are not confidence intervals. The 91.6% reference in Appendix D uses human–Codex pairs with complete training packages, rather than an autonomous model ceiling. Some groups regress, transfer coverage is narrow, and skill-generation costs can erase serving savings.

papers.title: AgentStream: How Well Do Self-Evolving LLM Agents Perform Under Streaming Tasks?

papers.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
papers.code_note: Author-linked survey repository and project introduction inspected on 2026-11-09. The artifact is a literature hub; no listed implementation, historical system or benchmark was independently executed for this review.

It distinguishes behavior-generated training signals consumed by an optimizer from direct scaffold edits, and treats skills as reusable updates across these substrates.

papers.title: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Complete twelve-page v1, Appendix A, two figures, five tables, Algorithm 1 and the anytime-valid argument read on 2026-11-10; figures, tables and gate equations visually inspected. No official research implementation was independently verified. Findings concern the paper’s reported experiments; no prompt-evolution runs, model calls or benchmark code executed.
papers.learning_signal: Paired candidate/incumbent correctness on development instances.
papers.mechanism: Wraps prompt-edit acceptance in a paired sequential betting test. Discordant candidate/incumbent outcomes update an e-process; an edit persists only if wealth crosses 1/alpha before the evaluation budget ends. Wealth resets for each candidate, while model weights stay fixed. Ground-truth dev answers supply the evidence; no additional model training is required.

A planted harmful instruction provides one large recoverable gain; a separate stochastic regime probes noise-driven commits. Controlled comparisons use five seeds, with three in stochastic and sensitivity studies. Statistical gates greatly reduce commit counts; fixed-n paired testing also performs well.

The audit is finite and uses temperature zero while stochastic dev evaluation uses 0.7. Some PACE commits are audit-labelled false, and small gains may be rejected. Planted repairs, one model family and an incompletely specified proposer limit system-level generalization; evaluation-count savings are not total-cost savings.

papers.title: Membrane: A Self-Evolving Contrastive Safety Memory for LLM Agent Defense
papers.code_note: Complete 35-page final EMNLP 2026 paper, Appendices A–E, twelve figures, twenty-three tables, full prompts and qualitative examples read on 2026-11-10; figures/tables visually inspected. Official Apache-2.0 release README and inventory inspected at 8d9c08aa352da0424b9d7c6122cc78e32b38477d. Requires model/embedding serving and additional reviewer/evaluation infrastructure. papers.learning_signal: Paired harmful/benign examples, guard decisions, and feedback about jailbreaks or false refusals.
papers.mechanism: Uses fixed language models to maintain contrastive safety cells pairing unsafe conditions with nearby benign exemptions. A planner creates, revises or deletes cells after paired interactions; schema checks constrain writes, and retrieval plus a critic supplies context for an external SAFE/UNSAFE guard. Separate prequential experiments allow reviewer-driven memory updates after each decision.

Residual harmful admissions remain high on several attacks, and online gains raise benign refusal. Contrastive online learning assumes supplied benign counterparts; poisoning robustness excludes fully adaptive prompt-and-store attackers and can hide denial-of-service effects. Transfer retention ratios are not absolute F1, and results do not establish deployment safety.

papers.title: On the Generalization Gap in Self-Evolving Language Model Reasoning
papers.code_note: Complete 26-page arXiv v2, Appendices A–C, four figures, thirteen tables, DPO definition and all verifier/reviser prompts read on 2026-11-10; quantitative figures and tables visually inspected. papers.mechanism: Uses one instruction-tuned model as both generator and verifier, collecting self-labeled preference pairs for full-parameter offline DPO. It compares thresholded voting, feedback-guided revision, repeated training on the same prompts and easy-to-hard curricula; retained changes are model weights. papers.title: PEAM: Parametric Embodied Agent Memory for Continual Skill Learning via Internalization of Experience in Minecraft
papers.code_note: Complete 13-page arXiv v2 and 14-page final Findings EMNLP 2026 paper read on 2026-11-10, including all four figures, five tables, algorithm and Appendices A–E. The final title and added within-adapter experiment were verified against the official venue and author page. The reported McNemar statistic and some interval values remain unreconciled with the stated 33-trial summaries. papers.mechanism: Uses a slow GPT-4o agent to acquire and verify executable Minecraft programs, then consolidates selected successes and matched failure–correction pairs into category-specific LoRA adapters on Qwen3-VL-8B. Isolated adapters prevent cross-category parameter changes but do not guarantee within-category retention. Trigger robustness mainly re-slices existing experience and retains fixed hyperparameters. Training cost is excluded from inference savings, hardware descriptions differ, and reported significance/intervals require clarification from raw trial records.

papers.title: MUSE-Autoskill: Self-Evolving Agents via Skill Creation, Memory, Management, and Evaluation

papers.code_note: Complete 12-page arXiv v1, all three figures, four tables, theorem/reduction and Algorithm 1 read on 2026-11-10; figures, tables and metric equations visually inspected. papers.title: MEMOREPAIR: Barrier-First Cascade Repair in Agentic Memory
papers.learning_signal: Explicit deletion, correction or interface-migration events, recorded dependencies and artifact-specific validation.
papers.mechanism: Withdraws an invalidated memory source and all influence descendants before repair. It rebuilds successor artifacts from retained support and staged predecessors, then uses a maximum-closure min-cut to select a cost-weighted, predecessor-closed repair plan. Only successors passing artifact-specific checks return to service; a chosen unlearning operator can also repair neural skills.
papers.evaluation: Full v1 studies deletion, correction and migration on ToolBench-derived and MemoryArena memory artifacts. It compares publication coverage and repair cost with exhaustive and greedy repair, tests provenance omissions and validation variants, and combines store repair with neural unlearning. The reported frontier uses three seeds; zero stale serving is conditional on the withdrawal/provenance contract.
papers.limitations: Requires complete causal provenance and adequate validators; dropping 1% of influence edges yields 17.7% leak in the reported check. Exact min-cut optimizes fixed values and costs, not a hard budget or future task success. The task-score diagnostic is constructed from artifact penalties rather than end-task accuracy, and repair cost excludes withdrawal. Event counts, implementation settings and numerical validation thresholds are insufficiently detailed for independent reproduction; neural repair is not exact erasure.

papers.title: Ask Only When Needed: Proactive Retrieval from Memory and Skills for Experience-Driven Lifelong Agents
papers.code_note: Complete 17-page final Findings EMNLP 2026 paper, Appendices A–F, four figures, seven tables, twenty-one equations and both algorithms read on 2026-11-10; figures/tables and proof equations visually inspected. Official venue identity verified. An official runnable implementation was not independently established; no policy training, simulator or extraction code executed.
papers.learning_signal: Environment rewards, paired retrieval/no-retrieval continuations, and interaction-length penalties.
papers.mechanism: Jointly trains an agent policy and expands factual, episodic, success, failure and comparative experience stores. After initial context retrieval, the policy can query memory as an action. Replayed prefixes create retrieval/no-retrieval continuations whose shaped outcome and length differences train retrieval timing and query content through GRPO.
papers.evaluation: The complete final paper evaluates ScienceWorld, ALFWorld and StuLife with a 7B agent and larger extraction model, plus 3B scaling, typed-store ablations and matched retrieval-controller baselines. It reports 73.5% ScienceWorld success with fewer interaction rounds; removing paired rewards or supervised initialization reduces performance in the tested configuration.

The formal analysis identifies a local noisy gradient signal rather than unbiased causal retrieval value or a policy-improvement guarantee. The experience store has no capacity bound, run/order uncertainty and exact online test-update accounting are underreported, and interaction/prompt savings exclude much of the learning pipeline.

papers.title: SkillFlow:Benchmarking Lifelong Skill Discovery and Evolution for Autonomous Agents

papers.learning_signal: Completed-task trajectories and externally supplied verifier-derived rubrics drive a fixed prompt that generates skill-file patches.

Library state resets between families; the execution models are not weight-trained. Skill use is detected through reads or calls of stored files.

papers.title: FlowEvo: Self-Evolving Agents through the Co-Evolution of Workflows and Executable Skills
papers.code_note: Complete 25-page arXiv v2, Appendices A–H, three figures, sixteen tables, algorithm and all prompts/records read on 2026-11-10. Official Apache-2.0 release 36e81efd4d1fdbabca7366200b15808ebef157fa and targeted code/math verification/retry paths inspected. papers.title: On Safety Risks in Experience-Driven Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Complete 25-page arXiv v1, Appendices A–D, nineteen figures, six tables, attribution equations and all cases/prompts read on 2026-11-10; plots, tables and equations visually inspected. papers.learning_signal: Benign execution experience and, in mixed-stream experiments, execution or refusal experiences retained by the evaluated frameworks.
papers.mechanism: Examines fixed-weight agents supplied with offline AWM workflows or online ReasoningBank experience. Benign interaction traces populate external memory; retrieval, memory size and manually controlled refusal/execution mixtures change later behavior. Length-expanded prompt controls and attribution analyses probe why safety outcomes differ.

papers.title: Combee: Scaling Parallel Prompt Learning for Self-Improving LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Complete 51-page arXiv v2 jointly reviewed on 2026-11-10, including all printed playbook excerpts and visual figure/table checks. Official COLM 2026 records verify the renamed title; the venue final body was not separately compared. Official ACE (Apache-2.0; Python >=3.10 and model/API dependencies) and GEPA (MIT) sources were inspected without execution. GEPA pull request 394 is merged; controller issue 395/pull request 492 remains open. No independent reproduction.
papers.learning_signal: Textual reflections from task executions, downstream scores, and measured iteration latency.
papers.mechanism: A parallel scaling layer around fixed ACE/GEPA prompt-learning rules. Agents produce reflections; duplication/shuffling and two-level grouped aggregation retain more local lessons before updating persistent prompts or playbooks. A controller chooses batch size from a profiled delay curve. Model weights and the underlying improvement rule remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: The reviewed v2 reports delay/quality comparisons on AppWorld, Terminal-Bench 2.0, Formula and FiNER. AppWorld Combee reaches 65.8% in seven minutes versus sequential ACE’s 58.1% in 86 minutes; the best naive batch reaches 65.4% in nineteen minutes. Terminal-Bench learning time falls from 42.4 to 2.4 minutes while accuracy falls from 37.9% to 35.6%. Some GEPA finance comparisons repeat optimization three times; playbook-quality scores use five judging runs.
papers.limitations: Speedups depend on the comparator and exclude offline Terminal-Bench trace generation and downstream context cost. LLM aggregation is not exactly associative or quality-preserving; several ACE settings lack independent optimization repeats. Playbook judging has no equal-length control or expert truth check, and printed entries are intentionally truncated. Single-profile synchronous batching does not establish asynchronous scalability. Some batch labels differ between figures and tables. Core GEPA aggregation is released, while its dynamic controller remains in an open pull request.

papers.title: APEX-EM: Non-Parametric Online Learning for Autonomous Agents via Structured Procedural-Episodic Experience Replay

papers.title: Retrieval-Augmented LLM Agents: Learning to Learn from Experience

Sparse and teacher-generated relevant memory often remains useful; self-experience benefits ALF but can strongly degrade ScienceWorld when added to useful memory.

Benefits depend on memory relevance and backbone; Gemma shows no hard-ScienceWorld gain. One retry does not establish continual heterogeneous experience accumulation. Dynamic retrieval and longer training can regress. Cross-paper scores are qualitative; seed variation in environment/retrieval is distinct from independent training replications, and cost tables omit memory collection and training.

papers.title: AutoSkill: Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning via Skill Self-Evolution
papers.code_note: Official current README inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents later document extraction, local skill management and SkillEvo components beyond the reviewed March 2026 paper. No code, datasets or skills were installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Recurring user queries, constraints and corrections are extraction evidence; assistant responses provide context rather than evidence of a successfully learned skill. Model judgments choose additions, merges or discards.
papers.mechanism: Uses fixed prompted modules to rewrite queries, retrieve instruction skills with hybrid dense/lexical search, and update a persistent versioned skill bank. A nearest-neighbor comparison guides maintenance; the generated artifacts are instructions supplied to later responses, without base-model training.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 reports 1,858 skill artifacts from four language/model subsets of long WildChat conversations, metadata distributions and multilingual examples. Versioned rewrite cases illustrate maintenance, but no controlled downstream task-performance or forgetting experiment is reported.
papers.limitations: Artifact and revision counts do not establish capability gains. Retrieval thresholds, extraction judgments, user/session boundaries and regression prevention lack controlled evaluation. Asynchronous maintenance is an architectural design, not measured zero overhead. Later repository replay/evaluation extensions must not be attributed retrospectively to this paper.

papers.title: EvoX: Meta-Evolution for Automated Discovery
papers.code_note: Complete 28-page arXiv v2, Appendices A–D, Algorithm 1, four figures, all result tables and search prompts read on 2026-11-10. Official Apache-2.0 SkyDiscover snapshot 0d932b690670a7e544388ad362e9876c8bd256a0 and EvoX-specific documentation inspected. Its documented strategy-score formula differs from the printed equation. papers.learning_signal: Task-evaluator scores, execution artifacts, and changes in population performance over search windows.
papers.mechanism: Co-evolves candidate solutions and executable search strategies within each optimization problem. Equal candidate counts do not match every model or evaluation cost, and AlphaEvolve comparisons use published results with unknown budgets. Main and appendix tables disagree on some numerical results. Strategy-window gains and illustrative breakthroughs do not independently identify causal optimizer improvement; broad optimality and ARC comparability remain unestablished.

papers.title: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
papers.code_note: Official preview README and formal-reasoning/search setup documentation inspected on 2026-11-09. papers.learning_signal: Earlier subtask actions and observations update episode-local persistent memory for later dependent sessions. The released formal-reasoning setup keeps model-judge outcomes out of memory by default.

Benefits and latency vary by backend and domain; prose, table aggregates and some case labels disagree. papers.title: SkillRL: Evolving Agents via Recursive Skill-Augmented Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Full 31-page arXiv v2, substantive Appendices A–F, checklist and all figures/tables/cases read on 2026-11-09; official NeurIPS poster record verifies acceptance. papers.mechanism: A teacher distills successes and failures into general and task-specific skills and generates a cold-start SFT dataset. GRPO then updates the acting policy while validation failures trigger skill additions. The policy and skill bank persist; the teacher, update procedure and optimizer remain fixed.

No error bars are reported, and benefits are not uniform across task categories or QA datasets. The measured full-prompt reduction is about 10%, distinct from the larger skill-compression claim.

papers.title: Group-Evolving Agents: Open-Ended Self-Improvement via Experience Sharing
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Task-success patterns, shared framework patches, failed-task traces and evaluation outcomes guide parent selection and offspring edits.
papers.mechanism: Selects pairs of agents using performance and behavioral novelty, shares their experience, and generates framework-level patches for both. A fixed reflection/evolution/archive procedure retains usable variants; the coding models are not weight-trained.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v1 compares staged SWE-bench/Polyglot evaluations against a DGM-style baseline with matched offspring counts and model schedules, then tests a selected agent across backbones. Five injected-bug trials supply the faulty agent with a bug-free peer.

The 88.3% headline and 88.0% transfer figure are unreconciled. Bug-repair results compare group and individual iterations, not a common compute unit.

papers.title: TAME: A Trustworthy Test-Time Evolution of Agent Memory with Systematic Benchmarking
papers.code_note: Complete 19-page final EMNLP 2026 paper, Appendices A–I, three figures, thirteen tables, equations and full prompts read on 2026-11-10. Official README/source inventory inspected at 521ba6534fc48c5b98b46c1b722edd140cc30eb7: core implementation and a small smoke-test example are present, while a full paper reproduction package and repository license were not verified. papers.learning_signal: Accurate binary task-outcome feedback, evaluator judgments of memory contribution, and model-generated trust annotations.
papers.mechanism: Maintains query-anchored experiences with utility estimates and textual trust notes. A fixed semantic filter and utility ranking select memories; an LLM evaluator assigns outcome-conditioned contribution scores that update reuse values. Successes and failures supply new experiences with cautionary annotations, while all model weights remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: The full final paper evaluates sequential science, mathematics, code and tool-use streams, then freezes memory for separate multidimensional trust probes. GPT-5.2 AIME improves by 14.6 points over the strongest listed baseline, while other utility and trust outcomes are mixed.
papers.limitations: Requires reliable task-correctness feedback and LLM judgments; contribution scores are not causal attribution. Memory insertion is not a formal safety gate, and TAME still loses trustworthiness in some domains. Pre-evolution scores differ across method wrappers, aggregation is domain-specific, and tuning/evaluation separation, independent-run uncertainty and total costs remain insufficiently specified. Human agreement does not establish deployment safety.

papers.title: Reasoning Cache: Continual Improvement Over Long Horizons via Short-Horizon RL
papers.code_note: Complete 31-page ICML 2026 final paper, all appendices, proof-generation extension, examples, prompts, figures and tables read on 2026-11-10. Official rc repository provides vLLM inference, modified verl/FSDP training and model/data links. READMEs and training-subtree Apache-2.0 license inspected at a pinned revision; root-wide licensing not established. Not installed, trained or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Correctness rewards on supplied mathematical prompt-answer pairs, with generated reasoning summaries reused during training.
papers.mechanism: Alternates bounded reasoning traces with compressed summaries, using the latest summary as within-problem state. Offline GRPO trains summary-conditioned reasoning from answer correctness; replayed summaries expose short rollouts to later-turn contexts. Model weights retain learned behavior, while inference caches restart for each problem.
papers.evaluation: The ICML final paper evaluates math and FrontierScience with reasoning budgets up to 512K. At 192K/256K caps RCT-4B reaches 66.3 HMMT, 58.0 IMO-AnswerBench and 34.1 FrontierScience, exceeding reported 4B autoregressive baselines on three of four benchmarks; it trails QwenThinking on AIME. Ablations support replay and reasoning-focused training. A separate 50K proof-training experiment improves judge-graded IMO-ProofBench scores.
papers.limitations: Inference gains use extra sequential computation; reasoning-token caps omit summary overhead. The 16K claim concerns each optimized rollout rather than total training cost, and standardRL controls match steps rather than complete FLOPs. Rewards are myopic and summaries can discard useful search history. Main final-answer metrics and separately judge-graded proofs do not certify reasoning correctness; independent training-run uncertainty is unreported.

papers.title: MemSkill: Learning and Evolving Memory Skills for Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Full 43-page arXiv v3, substantive appendices, checklist, all skills/prompts and figures read on 2026-11-09; official NeurIPS poster record verifies acceptance. README/source inventory at f65b797 inspected. Current setup documents four benchmark families, checkpoint reuse and concurrency caveats; AppWorld reproduction was not established. No installation, training or research execution.
papers.learning_signal: Downstream F1 or task success trains a separate skill-selection controller; hard training cases guide LLM-authored skill revisions.
papers.mechanism: PPO trains a lightweight controller to select memory skills for a fixed LLM executor. A fixed designer revises INSERT/UPDATE guidance from labeled hard cases; DELETE/NOOP primitives remain fixed in the supplied prompt. Skill-bank rollback uses late-cycle training rewards. Trace-specific memories and reusable memory skills are separate stores.

Higher success does not always reduce execution steps. Inference-cost savings exclude substantial API-heavy controller/skill preparation. Benchmark transfer does not establish continual deployment or privacy guarantees.

papers.title: Large Language Model Agents Are Not Always Faithful Self-Evolvers
papers.code_note: Official paper-linked repository and experiment/attribution README inspected on 2026-11-09; not installed or executed. Current documentation is not an independent reproduction of the ICML results.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Perturbs raw trajectories and condensed memories through removal, shuffling, corruption and replacement while keeping backbone weights fixed. Outcome sensitivity and final-turn gradient attribution probe whether experience influences an agent, rather than proposing a new learning algorithm.

Raw-trajectory perturbations often hurt interactive tasks more than condensed-memory changes.

Perturbations can be visibly irrelevant, task dependence is substantial, and repeated-run uncertainty is not reported. The appendix uses embedding-gradient norms as an attribution approximation, not a causal mechanism demonstration.

papers.title: Meta Context Engineering via Agentic Skill Evolution
papers.code_note: Current framework and separately linked mce-artifact READMEs inspected on 2026-11-09. No code, models or datasets were executed or installed.
papers.learning_signal: Labeled training rollouts and validation utility guide context revisions and skill selection. Files preserve earlier skills, context functions and evaluation history; models remain frozen.
papers.mechanism: A meta agent revises context-engineering skills, and a base agent executes them to build context files and retrieval code. A fixed history-informed evolutionary loop retains the better validation-scoring context. The reported generator uses a one-shot query-to-context interface.
