papers.title: Dr. Zero: Self-Evolving Search Agents without Training Data
papers.code_note: Official paper-linked README inspected on 2026-11-09; no index, model, data or training execution. Documentation requires a Wikipedia retrieval environment. Source availability is not independent reproduction.
papers.learning_signal: Solver exact matches against proposer-written answers supply difficulty and outcome rewards; seed passages and retrieved Wikipedia text ground generation without independently validating every answer.
papers.mechanism: Alternately trains a search-enabled question proposer and solver. Hop-grouped relative policy optimization normalizes proposer rewards across structurally similar questions, while GRPO trains the solver on generated QA. Model weights persist; the search corpus, retriever, prompts and reward design are externally supplied.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 compares 3B and 7B agents on seven short-answer QA benchmarks, with three-round dynamics, hop-mixture and reward ablations, repeated-evaluation summaries and a measured proposer-compute comparison. It reports competitive, but slightly lower average scores than supervised Search-R1.
papers.limitations: The 7B model declines in round three. Intended hop counts and matching generated labels do not certify factual correctness; a supplied question has a false premise. Reported uncertainty lacks some statistical details. Efficiency measurements concern proposer training, and QA results do not establish reliable long-form research, citation fidelity or indefinite improvement.

papers.title: AgentDevel: Reframing Self-Evolving LLM Agents as Release Engineering
papers.code_note: Official code availability was not established in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Programmatic scores or an implementation-blind LLM critic, trace-derived symptoms, and development-set pass-to-fail/fail-to-pass changes.
papers.mechanism: A fixed development engine generates diagnostic scripts and one prompt/code/tool-wrapper release candidate per iteration. A configurable regression gate retains accepted blueprints; the same development set drives diagnosis, promotion and stopping.
papers.evaluation: Reports improvements over an initial blueprint on SWE-bench Lite/Verified, WebArena and StableToolBench. Its WebArena ablation reduces regressions with gating while the ungated variant has a slightly higher final test score; cited external baselines were not rerun.
papers.limitations: No non-regression guarantee: accepted releases can still break cases, and gate thresholds, split sizes and repeated-run uncertainty are insufficiently specified. WebArena final scores differ between Table 1 (35.5) and Table 3 (34.2) without an explicit reconciliation. The test set is described as final-only, but iterative development reuses its training cases.

papers.title: MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Environment or benchmark outcome rewards update scalar utility estimates for retrieved experiences, while an LLM summarizes new episodes.
papers.mechanism: Keeps model weights fixed and stores intent, experience and utility triplets. Similarity filtering precedes utility-weighted ranking; a constant-step moving average updates the retrieved memories using the same outcome, and the memory bank expands.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 separates ten-epoch repeated-task learning on HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld and Lifelong Agent Bench from frozen-memory transfer on non-HLE splits. It includes retrieval ablations, cross-model memory reuse, two-domain merging, cost analysis and conditional estimator theory.
papers.limitations: HLE gains reflect repeated-question memorization, not held-out HLE generalization. At-least-once success is distinct from retained performance. Split-size reporting and validation selection need care; stationary-reward estimates do not prove absence of forgetting in an expanding memory system. Multi-memory credit assignment and false feedback remain unresolved.

papers.title: Agentic Memory: Learning Unified Long-Term and Short-Term Memory Management for Large Language Model Agents
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09: TrinityRFT training and model-based judging/distractor generation are documented. No installation, training or independent reproduction.
papers.learning_signal: A composite terminal reward combines graded task success, memory quality judged against reference information, and context-management proxies; the same group-normalized advantage is applied across steps.
papers.mechanism: Uses RL to train a language-model policy over six fixed long- and short-term memory operations. A three-stage curriculum creates memories, distracts the agent after resetting context, and asks a downstream question. Learned policy weights transfer across tasks; the training memory store resets between rollouts.
papers.evaluation: HotpotQA training transfers to four other benchmarks using two Qwen backbones. Appendix controls add comparable short-term tools and RL to earlier memory methods. Reported averages mix success, progress and graded-answer metrics; context-length and memory-quality ablations complement task scores.
papers.limitations: Operation-count and keyword-preservation rewards are proxies, not direct measures of useful maintenance or long-term retention. Terminal credit is not causal attribution to individual edits. Full lifecycle cost, repeated-training uncertainty and indefinite shared-memory retention are not established.

papers.code_note: Final 16-page Findings of EMNLP 2026 paper, complete substantive appendix, prompts, human validation and cost boundary read on 2026-11-09. The official repository at 92f2c3d contains only a README promising a later code release. Runnable implementation, configurations and reproduction remain unverified; no research code was executed.
papers.title: SkillRubricsRL: Evolving Skill-Grounded Agents with Rubric-Guided Reinforcement Learning
papers.learning_signal: Environment rewards and model-judged skill-fulfillment rubrics train the policy; perturbed-skill rollout outcomes update retrieval utilities.
papers.mechanism: Pairs skills with applicability-aware rubrics. Trajectory fulfillment contributes to policy reward, while skill-perturbation outcome differences update retrieval weights and the skill bank. After step 75, training mixes skill-on and skill-off prompts; rubric supervision remains active in both conditions.
papers.evaluation: The full final publication reports ALFWorld/WebShop results, skill-on/off comparisons, component ablations, merge histories and a three-expert check of 60 trajectory–skill pairs using clustered confidence intervals. Utility probes reuse the rollout group, with one full-skill anchor and perturbed skill contexts.
papers.limitations: Skill-off performance follows explicit skill-off training and does not by itself establish novel-task procedural transfer. Utility is context-dependent and the paper alternates replacement/dropout descriptions. Human validation is a small sample; policy-training uncertainty is not reported. Dollar estimates cover only rubric-judge calls, excluding updater fees and local training/rollout compute.

papers.title: PerMemSafe: Benchmarking Implicit Personalized Safety of Long Horizon Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Complete 19-page final Findings of ACL 2026 paper, Appendices A–G, seven figures, five tables, equations and all prompts read on 2026-11-10. Paper-linked Greysahy/permemsafe README, MIT license and requirements inspected at 58e73467bb70d773cd3d1133deed8b78b91dedeb. Release descriptions differ in domain count and scoring scale; availability is not reproduction. No research code executed or benchmark data downloaded.
papers.learning_signal: Changing implicit user-risk cues in constructed multi-session conversations, with annotated safety contexts for evaluation.
papers.mechanism: Benchmarks retrieval and response reasoning about implicit user risks, separating current-risk perception from tracking a previously resolved risk. Its SentinelMem method retains LLM-inferred safety facts, separate preference/risk profiles and explicit transitions linking a current fact to its predecessor. The evaluated adaptation changes external memory rather than model weights.
papers.evaluation: Complete final paper evaluates 750 constructed test instances from 276 synthetic conversations, with over 90% noise interactions, full-context models and five memory frameworks. GPT-4o grades risk awareness, provenance and helpfulness; agreement is assessed on 100 human-labeled cases. Stronger-model appendix results exceed the roughly 50% level of the main lightweight comparison.
papers.limitations: Safety labels measure rubric-based risk awareness and explicit resolution references, not observed harm or clinical outcomes. Synthetic rejection sampling selects a difficult distribution; queries sharing conversations are not independent users. The reported 23.8% gain is a relative contrast for one backbone, and SentinelMem does not lead every retrieval score. Human–judge agreement validates rubric consistency only; risk inference, deployment calibration and cost remain unresolved.

papers.title: COLLABMEM: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Collaborative Memory Operations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

papers.title: MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems

papers.title: Agent0: Unleashing Self-Evolving Agents from Zero Data via Tool-Integrated Reasoning
papers.code_note: Official series and Agent0 study READMEs inspected on 2026-11-09. The language and vision-language studies are separate; setup documents sandbox services and manual checkpoint selection between iterations. No installation, training, tool execution or reproduction was performed.
papers.learning_signal: Curriculum rewards combine answer self-consistency, capped tool-response counts and repetition penalties. Executor rewards match majority-vote pseudo-labels; code execution supplies intermediate feedback but does not independently certify those labels.

papers.title: Live-SWE-agent: Can Software Engineering Agents Self-Evolve on the Fly?
papers.code_note: Official paper-linked repository and configuration/release README inspected on 2026-11-09; not installed or run. Later README model scores are separate from the reviewed v3 experiments.
papers.learning_signal: Current-issue execution feedback and repeated prompts to consider useful tool creation guide the agent.

On the ablation subset GPT-5-Nano drops from 44% to 14%, and GPT-5-Mini also declines slightly. Baselines include imported results; repeated-run uncertainty is absent. Historical rankings and costs are not current guarantees.

papers.title: Self-Harmony: Learning to Harmonize Self-Supervision and Self-Play in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Full v2 and substantive Appendices A–M read on 2026-11-09. papers.title: OpenSIR: Open-Ended Self-Improving Reasoner
papers.code_note: Official paper-linked repository metadata and README inspected on 2026-11-09; not installed or trained. Current setup documentation does not establish reproduction of the v4 experiments.

papers.title: SPICE: Self-Play In Corpus Environments Improves Reasoning

papers.title: Search Self-Play: Pushing the Frontier of Agent Capability without Supervision

Official README documents veRL/SGLang, separate judge and retrieval services, and seed-data preparation. No installation, models, datasets or research code were executed.
papers.learning_signal: A fixed Qwen2.5-32B verifier and judge assess generated questions and solver answers against supplied seed answers. Solver failure rewards the proposer; valid questions are reused in a periodically cleared buffer.
papers.mechanism: Trains one model in proposer and solver roles using REINFORCE and GRPO. Search-grounded questions pass format rules and RAG verification with distractor documents. The main implementation reuses valid questions and clears its replay buffer every ten updates; learned behavior persists in weights.
papers.evaluation: Full v3 and Appendices A–E cover seven sampled QA benchmarks, several model families/sizes, continued training of search checkpoints, filtering and replay controls, algorithm/runtime trade-offs, and a failed negative-reward configuration. Outcomes are model-judged pass@1.
papers.limitations: 50,000 seed answers come from public training sets, and a stronger model supplies verification and judgment. Each benchmark uses 500 questions except Bamboogle’s 125, with fixed Wikipedia retrieval and ten search calls. RAG agreement cannot ensure unique valid questions. Reported gains lack independent training-seed uncertainty; rollout-time comparisons are not total-cost matches.

papers.title: MARSHAL: Incentivizing Multi-Agent Reasoning via Self-Play with Strategic LLMs
papers.code_note: Full v3 main text, substantive Appendices A–J, figures, reward/configuration details and raw results read on 2026-11-09; official repository README rechecked. ROLL/OpenSpiel and downstream MASLab setup are documented. No code, models or game evaluations were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Game outcomes plus engineered action-format and response-length rewards guide online reinforcement learning.
papers.mechanism: Updates a shared language model through cooperative and competitive self-play in fixed games. Turn-level returns are mean-centered within player-role groups. Learned weights transfer into fixed debate or cooperation workflows; the workflows themselves do not evolve.
papers.evaluation: Full arXiv v3 review covers three training games, three held-out games, seven reasoning benchmarks in single-agent/MAD/AutoGen settings, 4B/8B models, raw returns and all appendix controls. Authors report higher average downstream scores, alongside task-specific regressions.
papers.limitations: Game scores are normalized returns, not win rates; Hanabi evaluation uses self-play rather than unseen partners. Independent training-run uncertainty and matched generalist/specialist compute are not established. As printed, several MAD appendix ablations outperform full specialists, so component necessity is not uniform. Qualitative traces do not establish causal theory-of-mind gains.

papers.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
papers.code_note: Official repository linked in arXiv v3; README and public file tree inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents adaptation/evaluation modes and configurable feedback and deduplication. Current defaults differ from some paper settings; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Generated trajectories, execution feedback and helpful/harmful entry judgments; some experiments also supply reference answers. Feedback availability is varied explicitly.
papers.mechanism: Keeps model weights fixed while a Generator, Reflector and Curator maintain an itemized playbook. Local additions, counters and optional semantic deduplication replace complete rewrites. Offline adaptation and sequential predict-then-update adaptation are separate; the main online AppWorld result includes offline warmup.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v3 extends AppWorld and finance experiments with additional models, DDXPlus, judge-scored BIRD-SQL, feedback-corruption tests, update ablations and detailed token accounting. It reports both labeled and unlabeled conditions.
papers.limitations: Unlabeled online adaptation hurts FiNER in one main setting. BIRD-SQL scores use an LLM judge, not database execution. Lower adaptation cost coexists with more evaluation input tokens; caching benefits depend on deployment. Rollout counts differ across cost tables. Long-term retention, calibrated feedback and universal gains are not established.

papers.title: Mem-α: Learning Memory Construction via Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official paper-linked repository metadata, file list and README inspected on 2026-11-09; not installed or trained. README licensing claims were not confirmed by a root license file; no reproduction or paper-version equivalence is asserted.
papers.learning_signal: Downstream QA, tool-call formatting, compression and a fixed Qwen3-32B judge of memory-content type jointly reward policy training.
papers.mechanism: Reinforcement learning trains a Qwen3-4B writer to update core, episodic and semantic stores while processing history chunks. A fixed BM25 retriever and Qwen3-32B reader answer questions from the resulting memory; trained writer weights persist across histories.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v1 trains on eight data sources and evaluates 112 MemoryAgentBench contexts across retrieval, classification from examples and long-document summarization. It compares memory architectures, untrained writers and reward-component ablations, including a 474K-token history.
papers.limitations: Conflict revision is excluded; several task scores trail long-context or RAG baselines. Memory budgets and some readers differ across methods, and summary scoring uses keyword hits. The reward weight and balanced-training counts have reporting discrepancies; long histories do not establish procedural lifelong learning.

papers.title: Socratic-Zero : Bootstrapping Reasoning via Data-Free Agent Co-evolution
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not independently established in this review; this does not imply that no release exists.
papers.learning_signal: A fixed stronger teacher's correctness judgments, reference solutions, and failure-targeted generated problems.
papers.mechanism: A fixed stronger teacher judges solver attempts and expands the curriculum; DPO updates the solver, while weighted supervised learning distills the teacher into a generator. The displayed training algorithm still uses teacher-generated problems for the solver; generator utility is tested separately.
papers.evaluation: Three solver-training stages cover seven math and three general-reasoning benchmarks using Mean@32. A separate experiment trains a common student on different generators’ data and evaluates Mean@16; this is not a direct comparison of those generators as solvers.
papers.limitations: Uses 100 selected MATH seeds, 1,500 initial SFT problems and a Qwen3-235B teacher. The headline 20.2-point gain is over SFT, not the stronger synthesis baselines. Teacher-derived validity, small unquantified margins and inconsistent generator-score aggregates limit interpretation; teacher-free convergence is not demonstrated.

papers.title: ReasoningBank: Scaling Agent Self-Evolving with Reasoning Memory
papers.code_note: Official README at commit ed80611788292ea739f1effd31f16c53823b8a0d inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents WebArena/SWE-Bench integrations and a patched WebArena harness; current defaults were not reproduced or equated with the paper version.
papers.learning_signal: The agent’s backbone judges completed trajectories without reference answers in the main task stream. Multiple attempts provide contrastive evidence; a separate diagnostic injects label noise using ground truth.
papers.mechanism: Extracts short strategy notes from successes and failures, appends them to persistent memory, and retrieves notes from similar prior queries. Parallel or sequential memory-aware test-time scaling supplies additional experiences; model weights and the memory-update procedure remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: Reports WebArena, Mind2Web and SWE-Bench-Verified results, plus smaller-model, failure-memory, retrieval-size, judge-noise and token-cost analyses. Random-trajectory pass@1, model-selected best-of-N and oracle pass@k are distinct evaluations.
papers.limitations: Fewer interaction steps do not imply fewer total tokens: the reported cost breakdown includes a modest token increase over no memory. Simulated independent label flips do not capture every correlated judge error. Task-order sensitivity, long-term forgetting and repeated-run uncertainty are not established; strategy emergence is illustrated qualitatively.

papers.title: A-MemGuard: A Proactive Defense Framework for LLM-Based Agent Memory
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents AgentPoison-derived evaluation, retrieval backends and model-provider options. No attacks, research code, patient data, models or benchmark environments were executed or downloaded.
papers.learning_signal: An LLM judges query-grounded reasoning paths for consistency and unsafe intent; flagged paths become negative lessons consulted in later action checks.
papers.mechanism: Wraps a fixed agent with structured-path generation, consensus/safety validation and a separate lesson store. Query- and action-related retrieval brings previous failure patterns into pre-execution review. The main implementation uses model judgments rather than a pure majority vote.
papers.evaluation: The final ICML paper tests direct poisoning on StrategyQA/EHRAgent, indirect injection on MMLU, collaborative misinformation and adaptive attacks, including malicious-majority retrieval. It adds metric clarification, component ablations, retrieval-size sweeps and a batched-cost illustration.
papers.limitations: Strong poison-filtering reductions are not uniform end-to-end guarantees. ASR-t is one minus exact-match accuracy and includes ordinary model errors; benign accuracy also falls in some settings. Adaptive tests are bounded, and structural visualizations do not certify safety. More retrieved lessons can hurt utility; long-term protection and deployment cost remain uncertain.

papers.title: Memory-R1: Enhancing Large Language Model Agents to Manage and Utilize Memories via Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Gold-answer exact match rewards separately trained memory-manager and answer policies; explicit memory-operation labels are not required.
papers.mechanism: Uses PPO or GRPO to train a manager that adds, updates, deletes or retains memory entries, then trains an answer agent to select relevant content from retrieved memories. Manager training freezes the answer policy; answer training uses a fixed manager.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v5 trains on LoCoMo, reporting 152 training, 81 validation and 1,307 test questions, and transfers to MSC and LongMemEval without retraining. It compares backbones, GPT-5-trajectory supervised training, component removal, reward design and inference latency.
papers.limitations: Dialogue QA is the evidence setting, and gains vary by optimizer, backbone and metric. Judge rewards favor longer answers, while exact-match rewards favor concise ones. Appendix context-window counts disagree; repeated-training uncertainty and explicit dialogue-level split identifiers are not supplied in the inspected paper.

papers.title: A Benchmark for Self-Evolving Agents via Experience-Driven Lifelong Learning
papers.code_note: Final 41-page Findings of EMNLP 2026 paper, substantive appendices, full prompts, metrics and rollout records read on 2026-11-09. Official README, source inventory and metric calculator at 025741e inspected as text. The release retains earlier LAB documentation; final-paper version equivalence and a project-specific license were not established. No benchmark, model or research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task-state correctness, delayed information use and execution of earlier commitments at timestamp-only prompts. Evaluated variants add successful-trajectory fine-tuning, workflow/reflection memory, or supplied prompt and memory support.
papers.mechanism: Provides a synthetic, chronological campus environment with persistent calendars, bookings and other state, while raw model context resets between tasks. StuGPA combines exam, class and daily-life outcomes; retention and initiative metrics test tool-mediated information use and scheduled action.
papers.evaluation: The full final publication reports 1,284 instances across ten scenarios, default LLM baselines, an eight-student reference, oracle-context checks, rejection-sampling fine-tuning, AWM/Reflexion and context-engineering comparisons. The supplied skill prompt is authored guidance, not evidence of learned skill abstraction.
papers.limitations: One synthetic text domain and aggregate scores do not establish continual capability growth or intrinsic forgetting. Oracle context removes several bottlenecks simultaneously. Memory/prompt variants show mixed effects; independent-run uncertainty and the fine-tuning evaluation split are insufficiently specified. The current metric calculator differs from the final paper’s denominators and scoring formulas.

papers.title: Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs
papers.code_note: Author-linked repository README at commit 42fbbcac63dd58ed6856c0761357345a58e4f032 inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents both retrieval variants and separate retriever training; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task outcomes label stored plans. The implemented parametric variant trains a separate retrieval network with binary cross-entropy on success feedback; the underlying LLMs remain frozen.
papers.mechanism: A planner–executor agent retains final-state, plan and outcome cases. Retrieval uses fixed embedding similarity or a trained Q-network with top-k selection; this implementation simplifies the general multi-step soft-Q formulation to single-step prediction.
papers.evaluation: GAIA validation uses three passes with accumulating memory; test evaluation uses the validation-built bank. Separate QA transfer builds memory on four datasets before testing three others. Memory, planning, retrieval-size and model-choice ablations are reported.
papers.limitations: Repeated-task gains do not establish open-ended learning, and the no-memory baseline also improves across iterations. The stated weighted QA average conflicts with displayed values; model-judged partial-match scores are not established as equivalent to official leaderboards. Cross-system models and compute differ; uncertainty and lifecycle costs remain incomplete.

papers.title: A Comprehensive Survey of Self-Evolving AI Agents: A New Paradigm Bridging Foundation Models and Lifelong Agentic Systems
papers.code_note: Author-linked survey collection introduction and taxonomy inspected on 2026-11-09. This is a literature resource; its listings were not individually reproduced or treated as primary evidence for other papers.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable to the survey itself; its organizing loop compares task metrics, execution feedback, demonstrations and model-generated evaluations used by agent optimizers.
papers.mechanism: Connects system inputs, an agent system, environment feedback and an optimizer over a defined search space. It separates task-level from instance-level optimization and surveys model behavior, prompts, memory, tools, multi-agent topology and domain-specific workflows.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 synthesizes methods through August 2025 and discusses tool, web, software, scientific and multimodal benchmarks alongside model/agent judges. It proposes safety-first, performance-preserving evolution principles and identifies longitudinal evaluation, transfer, reward quality and cost as open problems.
papers.limitations: The broad optimization umbrella includes transient inference search and externally trained systems, not only persistent autonomous learning. Its three laws are design aspirations, not demonstrated guarantees. No reproducible screening funnel or pooled comparison is provided, and at least one cited method is misdescribed; primary-paper checks remain necessary.

papers.title: Temporal Self-Rewarding Language Models: Decoupling Chosen-Rejected via Past-Future
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09. It documents later corrections and pair-selection options that differ from paper pseudocode; its archived reproduction claims were not independently checked here. No research code, datasets, training or evaluation executed.
papers.learning_signal: Current-model preference scores rank outputs from initial, current and temporary trained models. Initialization uses external instruction/evaluation data and GPT-4o explanations; the separate online math extension uses correctness-filtered reference solutions.
papers.mechanism: Selects rejected answers from the lower-scoring initial/current candidates, trains a temporary model, then chooses better-scoring current/temporary answers. A second DPO stage starts again from the current model using these new pairs. Updated weights persist; the judge, candidate sources and selection rules define the learning signal.
papers.evaluation: The ICML 2026 paper compares five backbone/size configurations on three instruction benchmarks, four downstream tasks and a separate GRPO math extension. Two temporal iterations are compared with four standard self-rewarding iterations, alongside past/future and external-judge ablations.
papers.limitations: Matching DPO stage counts does not establish equal generation, judging or total compute. GPT-4o judging and response length affect the reported win rates; gains vary by metric and iteration. Conditional gradient analysis does not prove indefinite stable learning. Some tables and the current artifact pair rules disagree with the paper.

papers.title: Memp: Exploring Agent Procedural Memory
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and its public page inspected; not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Successful training trajectories initialize memory; benchmark success feedback selects, revises or filters later experience.
papers.mechanism: Combines detailed trajectories with abstract procedural scripts in an external memory bank. Similarity retrieval supplies guidance to fixed-weight agents; online variants append experience, keep successes or revise a retrieved procedure after failure.
papers.evaluation: The Findings of ACL paper evaluates TravelPlanner and ALFWorld with three models, comparing memory formats, retrieval keys and sequential update policies. It also transfers GPT-4o memories to Qwen2.5-14B and varies retrieval count.
papers.limitations: ALFWorld gains do not imply uniformly better planning: GPT-4o and Claude hard-constraint scores on TravelPlanner fall below no-memory baselines. Online updates rely on benchmark rewards; exact task counts, ordering and uncertainty are insufficiently specified in the paper. Cross-model reuse is not unrelated-domain transfer.

papers.title: R-Zero: Self-Evolving Reasoning LLM from Zero Data
papers.code_note: Official paper-linked README and training/release descriptions inspected on 2026-11-09; no models, datasets or research code run. Later R-Few work and older README scores are not substituted for the reviewed R-Zero v4 results.
papers.learning_signal: Solver majority votes provide pseudo-labels; disagreement, formatting and repetition signals reward the challenger. No independent correctness oracle supervises the main training loop.
papers.mechanism: Alternates GRPO updates of separate challenger and solver copies. The challenger proposes mostly mathematical questions; the solver samples answers, filters questions by agreement and trains toward its own majority answer. Updated model weights persist between rounds, with fixed human-designed prompts and reward rules.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v4 evaluates four backbones on seven mathematical and three general-reasoning benchmarks after three rounds, with additional iteration, shared-parameter, curriculum, supervised-data and pseudo-label diagnostics. Some contest results use mean accuracy over 32 samples; others use greedy decoding.
papers.limitations: Agreement is not correctness. Longer training eventually degrades and external-model diagnostics find worsening pseudo-label accuracy. Gains vary across tasks and several table/prose values conflict. The theoretical reward motivation does not guarantee a correct curriculum or indefinite improvement; pretrained knowledge and designed prompts remain inputs.

papers.title: A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents: What, When, How, and Where to Evolve on the Path to Artificial Super Intelligence
papers.code_note: Author-linked literature repository introduction and organization inspected on 2026-11-09; no research execution. TMLR publication reconfirmed from its official index; the precise OpenReview record currently presents an access challenge.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable to the survey itself; it distinguishes feedback type/source, demonstrations, population fitness, timing and update targets across surveyed systems.
papers.mechanism: Organizes agent changes by what evolves, when updates occur, how feedback drives them and where they are applied. A trajectory-conditioned system update formalism separates model, context, tools and architecture, while the survey includes both early feedback-driven mechanisms and stronger autonomous reconfiguration.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v4, matching the January 2026 TMLR title, synthesizes methods and proposes five evaluation goals: adaptivity, retention, generalization, efficiency and safety. It details short/long-horizon protocols, forgetting and backward-transfer probes, cost accounting, human intervention and benchmark coverage gaps.
papers.limitations: Survey inclusion does not prove persistent learning or recursive improvement. Protocols and gap claims are a historical synthesis, not a pooled experiment or certification. Some mechanism labels and numerical examples conflict with primary evidence or arithmetic; cost-per-gain also needs explicit treatment of zero or negative gains.

papers.title: GEPA: Reflective Prompt Evolution Can Outperform Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Training execution/evaluation traces and per-module feedback generate mutations; validation scores select candidates.
papers.mechanism: Mutates module instructions using trace reflection, retains complementary candidates through instance-wise Pareto selection, and optionally merges prompt sets from separate lineages. The executor weights and control flow stay fixed. A separate inference-time variant searches solutions on the target tasks themselves.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 compares six tasks on Qwen3-8B and GPT-4.1 Mini, including GRPO, prompt optimizers, selection ablations and cross-model transfer. It also reports kernel search and an adversarial instruction-following probe.
papers.limitations: Rollout budgets include validation but omit separate reflection calls; they are not total compute. GRPO is stronger on Qwen AIME; merging hurts several Qwen tasks. Main results lack independent search-run uncertainty. Kernel search is not held-out transfer, and the adversarial accuracy collapse largely reflects answer-format failure.

papers.title: EvoAgentX: An Automated Framework for Evolving Agentic Workflows
papers.code_note: Official repository inspected; the original URL redirects to ANative-Lab/EvoAgentX. No code was installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Task-specific reference scores and prompted feedback drive the integrated prompt and workflow optimizers.
papers.mechanism: Provides workflow generation, execution and evaluation around TextGrad, AFlow and MIPRO. Optimized prompts, demonstrations and executable workflow structures persist; the platform is an integration framework rather than a separately validated new learning algorithm. Its v2 memory optimizer remains under development.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 compares optimization choices on HotpotQA, MBPP and MATH, and adapts Open Deep Research and OWL on GAIA. Appendix examples show expanded reasoning prompts and an AFlow workflow with multiple candidate solutions and an ensemble.
papers.limitations: The paper does not fully specify actual optimization/evaluation splits, model settings, budgets or run uncertainty. Added calls are not controlled for total compute. MIPRO lowers MBPP from 69% to 68%; GAIA percentage gains are relative changes, unlike the benchmark-table percentage-point gains.

papers.title: SPIRAL: Self-Play on Zero-Sum Games Incentivizes Reasoning via Multi-Agent Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents Kuhn Poker training, evaluation and a later Tinker integration. No research code, model training or game evaluation was executed; current features are not assumed equivalent to the reviewed paper setup.
papers.learning_signal: Terminal game outcomes and role-conditioned advantage estimates.
papers.mechanism: A shared policy plays both roles in fixed language games and learns from terminal outcomes. Separate moving-average baselines for each game and role reduce update variance. Model weights evolve while game rules, rewards and the training procedure remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v3 tests game and academic-benchmark transfer, larger SFT-data controls, RLVR sequencing and three training seeds for the Qwen3-4B comparison. AIME/AMC use average accuracy over 32 samples; trace analysis uses a model judge to classify recurring reasoning patterns.
papers.limitations: Pattern frequencies and shorter traces do not establish causal skill transfer or reasoning loss. Some base-model evaluations use few-shot prompts, and data/compute budgets differ. Several appendix summaries conflict with detailed values. Engineered games, reported plateaus and bounded tests limit claims of indefinite improvement.

papers.title: Self-Adapting Language Models
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents separate knowledge and few-shot studies, GPU training requirements and an external grading API. No installation, model training or benchmark execution was performed.
papers.learning_signal: Training-time downstream performance after actual adaptation selects self-edits. ARC uses supplied target grids; knowledge evaluation uses reference answers and GPT-4.1 grading. External inputs, evaluation tasks and adaptation tools remain supplied.
papers.mechanism: An outer filtered-training loop learns to generate useful self-edits, while an inner gradient update adapts model weights. Knowledge edits generate training text; ARC edits select predefined augmentations and tuning settings. The update framework itself stays fixed.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 studies no-context SQuAD knowledge incorporation, joint continued pretraining, and 40 sampled adaptation configurations on eight preselected ARC evaluation tasks. Appendices add prompting, alternative-generator and proxy-reward comparisons; sequential edits test forgetting.
papers.limitations: ARC results are conditional on preselected solvable tasks. Stronger prompt baselines exceed the default learned-edit result, although training also improves those prompts. Some competing generators win in other settings. Sequential edits still forget; labeled evaluation and expensive candidate fine-tuning constrain broader continual learning.

papers.title: G-Memory: Tracing Hierarchical Memory for Multi-Agent Systems
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; setup instructions cover ALFWorld, PDDL and FEVER. Coverage of every paper experiment is not established; no research code executed.
papers.learning_signal: Completed multi-agent trajectories, task-resolution feedback and resource statistics drive memory updates; some configured agents have access to reference-based evaluation.
papers.mechanism: Maintains linked insight, query and interaction graphs with fixed models and orchestration. Similar-query retrieval, graph traversal, trajectory compression and role-specific projection supply memories at task onset; completed tasks update the hierarchy.
papers.evaluation: Three model backbones and three multi-agent frameworks are evaluated on five action/QA benchmarks, with adapted memory baselines, cost comparisons and component ablations. The largest advertised gain is against no memory, rather than the strongest memory baseline.
papers.limitations: Success, progress and exact-match scores differ across tasks. Task order, frozen-memory transfer splits and repeated-run uncertainty are insufficiently specified. The trajectory-length plot is not a cross-task learning curve; graph clusters do not establish causal transfer. Some baseline-gain and ablation interpretations conflict with displayed results.

papers.title: Self-Challenging Language Model Agents
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Generated executable checks provide binary rewards; passing examples and failure cases filter candidate tasks. Tool environments, prompt examples and verification scaffolding are supplied externally.
papers.mechanism: A fixed challenger explores tools and proposes Code-as-Task instructions and checks. In the main self-improvement setting, successful offline trajectories from the same 8B model are used for rejection fine-tuning of the executor; a separate setting distills 70B demonstrations. The challenger itself is not iteratively trained in these experiments.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v1 compares four environments from M3ToolEval and modified Tau-Bench, with four evaluation trials. It reports 12.0% to 23.5% average pass@1 for self-training and 32.2% with teacher distillation, plus verifier ablations, task/trajectory scaling, online-RL diagnostics and joint-training comparisons.
papers.limitations: Generated tests do not guarantee semantic correctness: filtering retains about 5% of Retail candidates and false negatives remain. Airline excludes no-action-success tasks, browsing is synthetic and improvements are mainly environment-specific. Prompt examples and baseline judging choices matter; online RL can collapse and annotation sample counts are inconsistent.

papers.title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents the outer loop, benchmark setup and experiment-log release. The paper’s full code-diff appendix was read, but no research code, model calls, containers or benchmarks were executed; current code was not matched to a paper-run commit.
papers.learning_signal: Coding-benchmark outcomes and logs inform a separate fixed o1 diagnostic model, which proposes changes for the selected coding agent to implement. The SWE-bench diagnosis prompt includes private-test information from prior evaluations.
papers.mechanism: Selected coding agents modify their own implementation, and an archive retains functional variants, including weaker candidates that may support later improvements. Agent tools and workflows evolve; foundation models, diagnostic prompting, archive management and parent selection remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v3 reports staged SWE-bench and Polyglot search evaluations, full-Polyglot and cross-benchmark/model transfer tests, fixed-modifier/latest-agent/greedy baselines and three Polyglot runs. A separate three-task study examines tool-use hallucination and objective hacking.
papers.limitations: The 50% SWE-bench result is on a 200-task subset used during search. Staged selection, private-test diagnostic feedback and higher compute than baselines qualify the main curves; cross-benchmark tests provide stronger transfer evidence. A perfect hallucination score was obtained by bypassing logging-based detection, not by solving hallucination.

papers.title: LifelongAgentBench: Evaluating LLM Agents as Lifelong Learners
papers.code_note: Official paper-linked repository and setup/experiment README inspected on 2026-11-09; no containers, datasets or model runs executed. Source availability does not verify all generated task labels.
papers.learning_signal: Environment-verified task outcomes determine which recent successful trajectories enter replay; group variants vote over actions conditioned on separate experience subsets.
papers.mechanism: Sequences tasks with overlapping SQL, shell-command and knowledge-graph skills and retains interaction histories for fixed-weight agents. Database tables and operating-system containers reset between tasks. Group self-consistency splits replay into multiple inference contexts and votes on the next action.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v3 contains 500 database, 500 operating-system and 396 knowledge-graph tasks. It varies replay size, model backbone, task difficulty and grouping, reporting task success and average input length alongside format, context and execution-failure examples.
papers.limitations: Replay can hurt stronger baselines or exhaust memory. Grouping shortens each context but adds inference calls, so it does not establish equal-compute efficiency. Shared skills do not imply persistent environment state, and the results do not directly measure forgetting over revisited old tasks. Some appendix error explanations are incorrect.

papers.title: Absolute Zero: Reinforced Self-play Reasoning with Zero Data
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it separates the original paper branch from newer development code and warns about the raw executor. No code execution, model download, training or reproduction was performed.
papers.learning_signal: Python execution checks sampled task/answer agreement. The proposer reward depends on eight sampled solver attempts, favoring difficult but sometimes solvable tasks; it is a proxy for learnability, not measured future improvement.
papers.mechanism: A shared pretrained model proposes and solves three kinds of code-reasoning tasks. Joint reinforcement learning updates both roles, and a buffer retains valid generated tasks for subsequent proposals and training. Task formats, verification and the optimization procedure remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v3 compares coding and mathematics benchmarks across model families and sizes, with task/proposer ablations, high-pass@k coverage and MMLU-Pro results. Appendices report unsuccessful curriculum, reward and preprocessing alternatives.
papers.limitations: Zero data concerns new curated post-training tasks, not pretraining or human-designed rules. Finite execution checks do not prove program equivalence or faithful reasoning; retained globals can leak answers. Some benchmarks regress, and model/data budgets differ across baselines. Bounded results do not establish unlimited or safe autonomous improvement.

papers.title: Mem0: Building Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Conversation messages, summaries and LLM decisions about whether candidate facts add, update, contradict or duplicate stored information.
papers.mechanism: Extracts facts from recent exchanges and background summaries, then updates an external memory store through add/update/delete/no-op decisions. The graph variant stores entities and relations and can invalidate obsolete edges; neither variant trains model weights during memory management.
papers.evaluation: LoCoMo conversational QA excluding adversarial questions, with lexical metrics, repeated judge scoring and query-time latency/token measurements. The full-context baseline has higher overall judge accuracy; graph memory helps some categories but trails base Mem0 on single- and multi-hop questions.
papers.limitations: Query-time savings do not include the full cost of building and updating memory. Hosted/manual baselines and imported results require version-matched protocols; A-MEM category labels differ across the compared documents. The permissive judge and exclusion of unanswerable questions limit factuality/abstention conclusions. Production readiness is not independently established.

papers.title: RAGEN: Understanding Self-Evolution in LLM Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official current README inspected on 2026-11-09; it distinguishes original RAGEN from later RAGEN-2 and related releases. No installation, training, model or environment execution; the current branch is not treated as a reproduction of arXiv v2.
papers.learning_signal: Task rewards on multi-turn trajectories drive policy updates. Within-prompt reward variability is used for filtering; entropy and gradient statistics diagnose training behavior.
papers.mechanism: StarPO organizes trajectory collection and PPO/GRPO updates to model weights. StarPO-S tests variability-based prompt filtering and gradient changes, including KL removal and asymmetric clipping. These are externally specified training interventions, not agent-written changes to the learning algorithm.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 studies Bandit, Sokoban, FrozenLake and WebShop, with model-size, rollout-frequency, action-budget and distribution-shift analyses. It reports collapse and spurious reasoning, plus an appendix comparison where supervised learning from search-generated trajectories outperforms RL on Sokoban.
papers.limitations: Stochastic reward variance is not calibrated knowledge uncertainty, and shorter reasoning text does not alone prove loss of reasoning ability. Stabilization benefits vary by task and optimizer. Small environments, limited repeat-run reporting and inconsistent horizon descriptions constrain generalization. The current RAGEN-2 software and paper are distinct from this study.

papers.title: A Self-Improving Coding Agent
papers.code_note: Official README and selected benchmark code at ed8275dca4d3c5dbf77229964351fe9b424797dc inspected on 2026-11-09. The current SWE scorer uses binary harness resolution, but its default subset differs from the paper. No code, containers or benchmarks were executed.
papers.learning_signal: A fixed utility combines benchmark scores, dollar cost and elapsed time. Archived results and traces guide subsequent code modifications; no model-weight training is performed.
papers.mechanism: Selects the best prior agent from an archive to modify its own Python implementation, then evaluates the resulting agent. Tools, prompts and orchestration can persist into later modification attempts, while the outer archive-selection and evaluation loop stays fixed.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 reports a fifteen-iteration coding run on reused SWE-bench Verified and LiveCodeBench subsets plus synthetic editing/navigation tasks. A separate AIME/GPQA run finds little improvement. Per-iteration scores, costs and times reveal regressions as well as gains.
papers.limitations: No independently held-out final task set or fixed-modifier ablation is reported. Short timeouts make editing efficiency a major contributor; best-so-far utility is not monotonic task improvement. Paper and current-code subset settings differ, and broader run variance remains unclear. Observability is not a demonstrated safety guarantee.

papers.title: A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Official system repository inspected; it distinguishes this reusable memory package from the separate paper-evaluation repository. Neither was executed.
papers.learning_signal: New conversation content and LLM-generated contextual descriptions, tags, relationship decisions and neighbor updates.
papers.mechanism: Creates atomic notes, retrieves candidate neighbors by embedding similarity, links relevant notes, and revises neighboring contextual attributes. Persistent external notes change subsequent retrieval; model weights remain fixed.
papers.evaluation: LoCoMo and DialSim conversational QA; six main-table models plus three appendix models, link/evolution ablations, retrieval-size sweeps and storage/retrieval scaling. Category-level comparisons require resolving the version-specific table-label differences described below.
papers.limitations: Retrieval k is tuned by model and question category; the checklist reports no repeated-run significance analysis. Table 1 in v5 and v11 assigns different category names to unchanged score columns, and v11 retains a twofold multi-hop claim inconsistent with its displayed labels. Category-specific gains remain uncertain until the labeling is reconciled.

papers.title: Agent-R: Training Language Model Agents to Reflect via Iterative Self-Training
papers.code_note: Paper-linked repository redirects to ByteDance-Seed/Agent-R. README and trajectory-construction code at 82fcc1ca7873b460949ed49022146dd988c32e31 inspected on 2026-11-09; no code, environments or training were executed, and paper-result reproduction is not established.
papers.learning_signal: Environment terminal rewards select contrasting tree-search paths; the current actor identifies a revision point. Training also includes ShareGPT data and manually written revision connectors.
papers.mechanism: Builds synthetic recovery trajectories by truncating a bad branch and appending a good continuation. Iterative supervised training updates the actor on good and revised trajectories, with loss focused on the revision and continuation. The search, selection and training procedure itself stays fixed.
papers.evaluation: Three Llama-3.1-8B training rounds evaluate WebShop/ScienceWorld reward and TextCraft success. Separate tests continue truncated failures from the original model, and analyses examine repeated actions, revision positions and multi-task training.
papers.limitations: Earlier self-identified errors are not independently measured localization accuracy. Spliced trajectories assume compatible environment states; the inspected construction code assembles logs without replaying the combined path at that stage. Metrics, baseline training and data budgets differ; repeated-run uncertainty and generalization beyond the three environments remain unestablished.

papers.title: LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Constructs 500 curated questions with annotated evidence embedded in scalable user-assistant histories, testing extraction, multi-session reasoning, updates, temporal reasoning and abstention. It separates indexing, retrieval and reading, then varies their designs without training a continually improving policy.
papers.evaluation: Studies roughly 115k-token and 1.5M-token histories, retrieval granularity, fact-expanded keys, temporal filters and reader prompts. A GPT-4o judge is checked against humans on thirty responses per question type from each of two answer models; retrieval and answer scores are reported separately.
papers.limitations: Histories combine simulated/human-edited evidence with sampled background sessions. The 97-question commercial-system study used shorter histories in August 2024 and omitted several abilities. Reader and query-model choices affect gains; retrieval correctness can require obsolete evidence unnecessary for a correct updated answer. Recall scores do not establish procedural learning.

papers.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents APIs, operators and evaluation resources, and notes possible operator issues after migration from MetaGPT. No research code, datasets or benchmark runs were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Validation-set scores and execution logs, including expected answers, guide a fixed LLM optimizer. Code workflows can also use supplied public tests and generated tests during solution refinement.
papers.mechanism: Searches Python workflow structure and custom prompts with an MCTS-inspired selection/expansion loop. Actual experiments fix models, temperatures and output formats and provide reusable operators. Selected workflows and tree-organized experience persist; the optimizer itself is unchanged.
papers.evaluation: Six reasoning/QA/code benchmarks use a seeded validation/test split, five validation evaluations per candidate and three test evaluations. Studies include cross-model workflow transfer, a GSM8K operator ablation, inference-cost comparisons and small judged writing/idea-generation cases.
papers.limitations: Repeated executions do not measure independent search-run variance. Gains mix task metrics, and inference-cost comparisons exclude search costs. Algorithm descriptions differ in selection details; the theoretical discussion does not prove finite global optimality. Open-ended cases remain small and do not independently establish novelty or exact constraint satisfaction.

papers.title: AgentSquare: Automatic LLM Agent Search in Modular Design Space
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Task-performance evaluations and an in-context predictor conditioned on examples of previously evaluated module combinations.
papers.mechanism: Alternates code-level module evolution with recombination of planning, reasoning, tool-use and memory modules. Novel modules receive environment evaluation; recombinations use an LLM surrogate. Module pools and scored designs persist within a fixed external search procedure.
papers.evaluation: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o comparisons on WebShop, ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, M3ToolEval, TravelPlanner and PDDL, with module ablations, surrogate-versus-observed plots and search/execution-cost analyses. Reported metrics differ across tasks: success, reward, progress and micro pass rate.
papers.limitations: Search remains constrained by standardized interfaces. Execution-cost plots exclude search costs, which are tabulated separately. The inspected paper does not specify a separate held-out search/test partition or independent-run uncertainty; surrogate correlation is not a guarantee that novel designs generalize.

papers.title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Validation-task scores and error information guide changes to the solver and its self-modification logic.
papers.mechanism: Uses runtime code inspection and monkey patching to revise both task-solving functions and parts of the improvement process. Human-specified goals, interfaces and initial tools provide the starting conditions; the experiments do not train the underlying model weights.
papers.evaluation: The ACL paper searches six times per task, up to thirty iterations, with a GPT-4o optimizer on DROP, MGSM, MMLU and GPQA. The constrained executor uses GPT-3.5; unrestricted results can invoke stronger models. Game-of-24 and robustness studies provide further diagnostics.
papers.limitations: Baselines are imported from prior work, and test-bootstrap intervals do not measure search-run variation. In 100 MGSM trials, 14% finish worse and 4% terminate unexpectedly. Unrestricted scores and historical cost estimates are not controlled equal-resource comparisons or proofs of unlimited improvement.

papers.title: Training Language Models to Self-Correct via Reinforcement Learning
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Ground-truth answer checks and unit tests reward self-generated training traces; no correctness oracle is supplied for test-time revision.
papers.mechanism: Trains one model through two-turn online RL: first constrain initial answers while learning revisions, then optimize both turns with a progress bonus. The learned weights persist across problems; each test-time revision remains a within-problem operation.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v2 evaluates Gemini models on MATH500 and HumanEval after MATH/MBPP training, with offline MBPP-R repair, component ablations and repeated-attempt tests. MATH training incorporates 4,500 original test problems while reserving 500 for evaluation.
papers.limitations: The 15.6-point MATH headline is improvement in the correction delta, not final-answer accuracy. Training uses oracle rewards and training-reward checkpoint selection; code first-attempt accuracy can decline. Only two attempts are trained, and answer-level reward does not verify every reasoning step.

papers.title: Agent Workflow Memory
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; separate WebArena and Mind2Web offline/online entry points are documented. Source availability is not an independent reproduction of the final paper.
papers.learning_signal: Annotated offline demonstrations or completed online trajectories accepted by a model-based success evaluator; model weights stay fixed.
papers.mechanism: Abstracts reusable subtask workflows and inserts them into agent context. Offline workflows are induced before evaluation; online workflows accumulate after completed tasks. Experiments group tasks and workflow stores by website. Executable workflow shortcuts are a separate variant.
papers.evaluation: The final ICML paper evaluates WebArena, a cross-template subset and Mind2Web, with representation, mixed-memory, task-order and cost analyses. Its Mind2Web headline improvement is in step success, distinct from whole-task completion.
papers.limitations: Combining offline and online memories can hurt; executable shortcuts improve step scores while reducing whole-task success in the displayed table. Task-order evidence covers small website groups. Model identifiers and some baseline rows conflict across the final paper, limiting exact comparison claims. Learned success judgments can admit faulty workflows.

papers.title: Automated Design of Agentic Systems
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Validation-task scores, runtime errors and an archive of earlier code designs; the pretrained meta-agent proposes and reflects on candidates.
papers.mechanism: A fixed meta-agent writes executable forward functions, checks novelty, repairs execution errors, and archives designs with scores. Search changes prompts and control flow in task agents; the outer search algorithm and model weights are fixed.
papers.evaluation: ARC grid-transformation code and DROP, MGSM, MMLU and GPQA; cross-domain/model transfer and empty-archive controls. ARC uses 20 validation and 60 test problems with grids at most 5 by 5; reported intervals are bootstrap estimates, not independent search-run variation.
papers.limitations: Experiments concern bounded question-answering tasks; continual deployment and optimization of the meta-agent are proposed future work. ARC transfer candidates were selected by source test accuracy. Transfer does not benefit every agent/model pairing, and performance-only search does not establish equal-cost superiority.

papers.title: Recursive Introspection: Teaching Language Model Agents How to Self-Improve
papers.code_note: Official author project and final-paper checklist identify this repository. README inspected on 2026-11-09; it documents FastChat-based reward-weighted training and math evaluation. No code, model or benchmark execution; complete final-paper reproduction is not claimed.
papers.learning_signal: Training uses reference-answer checks to select better responses from the learner or a stronger teacher. The main teacher-assisted setup includes a knowledge-boosting stage; the self-distillation experiment is separate.
papers.mechanism: Converts a problem into a sequence of attempted answers and trains a correction policy with reward-weighted learning on accumulated rollouts. At deployment, fixed-weight revisions concern the current problem: oracle stopping or checker-free majority voting are alternative protocols.
papers.evaluation: The final NeurIPS paper includes math comparisons, up to ten-turn evaluation, cross-dataset and model-transfer analyses, and added MBPP/CoNaLa results. Controls compare sequential and parallel sampling, training-data composition and preservation of correct answers.
papers.limitations: Equal sample counts do not guarantee equal token or latency budgets. The single-iteration self-distillation variant trails parallel sampling from the same trained model. Some first-turn scores regress; the checklist reports no repeated training runs. Code-task protocols are less detailed than math experiments, and bounded correction is not recursive improvement of the training algorithm.

papers.title: Symbolic Learning Enables Self-Evolving Agents
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: Prompted task assessments, optionally supplied with reference answers and scores, produce textual feedback for upstream nodes.
papers.mechanism: Records an execution trajectory, propagates natural-language critiques backward, and edits prompts, tool definitions and pipeline configuration with fixed LLMs. Invalid edits are retried; a rollback check reevaluates the current training example. Batched feedback can guide a shared update.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v1 presents GPT-3.5/GPT-4 experiments on HotpotQA, MATH and HumanEval with tools disabled, plus GPT-4-judged creative writing and five software-development tasks scored for executability. Appendix prompts illustrate feedback and configuration edits.
papers.limitations: Textual gradients are analogies, not derivatives or convergence guarantees. Split sizes, optimization budgets and repeated-run uncertainty are insufficiently specified. Same-example rollback does not establish held-out improvement; GPT-3.5 HumanEval trails DSPy. The proof-of-concept does not demonstrate sustained deployment learning.

papers.title: TextGrad: Automatic "Differentiation" via Text
papers.venue: Nature 2025; journal title: Optimizing generative AI by backpropagating language model feedback
papers.code_note: Official repository landing page inspected; no installation or execution performed.
papers.learning_signal: LLM critiques of intermediate variables, labels, local test outcomes and simulator-derived objectives, depending on the application.
papers.mechanism: Backpropagates textual feedback through a computation graph and rewrites selected variables using a fixed LLM optimizer. Reusable prompt optimization and within-instance answer/code/molecule/plan refinement are separate settings; textual gradients are an analogy, not derivatives of model weights.
papers.evaluation: Reviewed arXiv v1: 39 LeetCode problems over five seeds, GPQA/MMLU refinement, three prompt-optimization tasks, molecular simulations and five retrospective treatment plans. Prompt search uses validation gates; GPQA combines three refinements with majority voting.
papers.limitations: The later Nature article is not assumed equivalent to v1. LeetCode prose and Table 1 disagree on baseline accuracy. Compute and voting complicate attribution; simulation scores and retrospective dose metrics establish neither drug safety nor clinical effectiveness. No implementation was executed.

papers.title: ReST-MCTS*: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
papers.code_note: Official repository README, setup, data-release and training descriptions inspected on 2026-11-09; no research code, datasets or models executed/downloaded. README value-training learning rates differ from the reviewed paper and were not silently reconciled.
papers.learning_signal: Known final answers verify sampled solutions; search reachability and distance produce intermediate value targets. Science initialization also assumes supplied step-by-step solutions are correct and weak-model continuations are wrong.
papers.mechanism: Uses a learned value model to guide tree search with step expansion, rollout and self-criticism. Successful traces fine-tune the policy; inferred values from searched trees train the reward model for the next round. These are persistent parameter updates, distinct from test-time search alone.
papers.evaluation: ArXiv v3 reports two training rounds across three backbones on MATH, GPQA Diamond and CEval-Hard, plus GSM8K/MATH500 verifier comparisons and SciBench/SciEval search studies. Token-budget curves and a separate runtime table compare search efficiency.
papers.limitations: Oracle answers and initialization data remain supervision. Reaching a correct final answer does not prove every preceding step valid. Average gains mask task regressions, and matched completion tokens do not imply matched total compute or latency. Some reported values/settings conflict; broad agent tasks and indefinite learning are untested.

papers.title: Re-ReST: Reflection-Reinforced Self-Training for Language Agents
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; it explicitly points to HotpotQA and GQA implementations. Coverage of every paper experiment was not established, and no research code was executed.
papers.learning_signal: Reference-answer correctness, environment completion and provided unit tests filter training examples; image-generation feedback comes from a visual evaluation model. Optional GPT-4-initialized comparisons are separate.
papers.mechanism: Trains a separate reflector on failed/successful sample pairs, uses one reflection step to repair rejected generations, and fine-tunes the agent on accepted original and repaired trajectories. Improvement persists in model weights; the main inference path uses the agent without reflection.
papers.evaluation: The final EMNLP paper studies HotpotQA, ALFWorld, MBPP, visual programming and text-to-layout/image generation. Ablations compare more initial samples, trained versus untrained reflection, DPO and a separate test-time self-consistency variant.
papers.limitations: Self-training still needs supplied tasks and training-time feedback. MBPP prompts contain provided unit tests, and visual feedback is not human ground truth. Sampling-efficiency comparisons do not fully account for reflector training. Seed-level uncertainty and broad retention are not established; main training-only reflection and test-time variants should remain distinct.

papers.title: Is Model Collapse Inevitable? Breaking the Curse of Recursion by Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data
papers.code_note: ArXiv v2 and its substantive appendices were read in full on 2026-11-09. An official runnable implementation was not established; the author page’s PDF link returned 404 and the final OpenReview body was access-restricted. No training, models or research code were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Models train on targets or samples generated by earlier models, retaining the original reference corpus and all successive synthetic batches in the accumulation condition. The data-retention rule is fixed.
papers.mechanism: Contrasts latest-generation replacement with accumulation of all preceding datasets. In a repeated-design linear regression setting, older data reduce each generation’s added-noise contribution sufficiently to bound expected excess error.
papers.evaluation: The detailed arXiv v2 review covers small transformer pretraining on TinyStories, GeoDiff molecular conformations, CelebA VAEs, exact linear-model analysis and dataset-size/temperature/training ablations. Indexed official records establish later COLM 2024 publication; its final body was inaccessible in this pass.
papers.limitations: The bound assumes reused covariates, independent additive noise and underparameterized regression. Growing datasets alter compute and storage; size-matched replacement does not match all generation costs. VAE diversity still degrades, and TinyStories is itself generated text. Bounded error is not unchanged quality or a guarantee for arbitrary self-learning agents.

papers.title: Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents
papers.code_note: Official repository linked and inspected; not installed or executed.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable: analysis or evaluation resource.
papers.mechanism: Creates persona- and event-grounded simulated conversations, then uses human editing to repair consistency and image alignment. The benchmark tests QA, event summarization and multimodal dialogue generation; a separate training corpus supports the multimodal model experiments.
papers.evaluation: The ACL paper reports ten edited conversations and 1,986 QA items, averaging 16,618 tokens per conversation. It compares truncated/long-context models and RAG, then MiniGPT-5 variants trained on fifty additional unedited conversations. Experiments report a single inference run per model.
papers.limitations: Primarily synthetic English conversations and web images do not reproduce real longitudinal user histories or persistent personal imagery. QA mostly substitutes image captions and uses lexical scoring. The preprint/project reports different statistics; pin the publication, data artifact and evaluator rather than combining those descriptions. This tests memory use, not autonomous skill acquisition.

papers.title: TroVE: Inducing Verifiable and Efficient Toolboxes for Solving Programmatic Tasks
papers.code_note: Official README inspected on 2026-11-09; task-specific entry points and the GQA perception-service dependency are documented. No generated tools, research code, models or benchmark environments were executed.
papers.learning_signal: Agreement among executed candidate answers, a program-complexity proxy and observed tool reuse; reference answers are used for evaluation rather than per-task tool admission.
papers.mechanism: Samples programs in import, create and primitive-only modes, chooses a frequent executable answer with simplicity tie-breaking, and retains its reusable functions. Periodic frequency-based trimming also regenerates earlier solutions affected by removed tools. The model and toolbox-management procedure stay fixed.
papers.evaluation: The final ICML paper covers eleven math, table-QA and visual-reasoning datasets, ordering/selection/rectification ablations, and a six-person verification study. Main results select the best of five runs; some external baselines reuse previously published scores.
papers.limitations: Execution agreement is not correctness verification, and best-run reporting does not estimate typical performance. Retrospective regeneration differs from scoring each streaming prediction once. Supplied primitives and demonstrations matter; complexity is an AST-based proxy. Human verification improves on the tested sample, but broader reliability, lifecycle cost and retention remain unestablished.

papers.title: Self-Rewarding Language Models
papers.code_note: Official runnable code was not verified in this source review.
papers.learning_signal: Human-ranked seed data initialize answering and evaluation; the resulting model scores its own candidate answers to create preference pairs.
papers.mechanism: Alternates answer generation, self-judging and DPO updates, changing the shared answering/reward model. The main experiment uses a fixed Llama-2-Chat prompt generator and Claude-2 checkpoint selection, so the loop retains external design and supervision dependencies.
papers.evaluation: The ICML paper studies a Llama-2-70B seed model and two main DPO rounds using GPT-4 judging, fifty blinded author-rated prompts, MT-Bench, NLP tasks and held-out human preference rankings. A fourth model receives a further AlpacaEval check with smaller gains.
papers.limitations: Responses become longer, potentially influencing preference scores. Gains concentrate outside mathematical reasoning, and several NLP scores regress. Reward-ranking agreement is not correctness or safety assurance; finite iterations, uneven training-data volumes and external checkpoint selection limit claims of autonomous continual improvement.

papers.title: Self-Play Fine-Tuning Converts Weak Language Models to Strong Language Models
papers.code_note: Official repository page checked; code and training were not executed.
papers.learning_signal: Existing reference demonstrations are treated as preferred to responses sampled from the preceding model, without fresh per-pair preference labels.
papers.mechanism: Optimizes a contrastive log-probability-ratio objective against the previous model, then samples a new opponent dataset from the updated weights. The experiments reuse 50,000 UltraChat prompts with API-generated reference answers; later rounds mix current and preceding generated responses.
papers.evaluation: The ICML paper evaluates four rounds on Zephyr-7B using Open LLM Leaderboard tasks, with additional MT-Bench, BBH and OpenBookQA results, data/epoch ablations and optional later DPO. Average gains diminish, and some task scores remain below the SFT baseline.
papers.limitations: Experimental reference answers are synthetic, despite the human-demonstration framing; they remain the fixed target distribution. Idealized theorems assume realizability and global optimization, not guaranteed finite-SGD convergence. DPO comparisons differ in data and supervision; independent training-run uncertainty is not reported.

papers.title: When Can LLMs Actually Correct Their Own Mistakes? A Critical Survey of Self-Correction of LLMs
papers.code_note: No implementation link independently inspected for this entry; this does not establish that none exists.
papers.learning_signal: Not applicable to the survey itself; it distinguishes prompted feedback, external tools/knowledge and trained correction models in the reviewed literature.
papers.mechanism: Organizes inference-time correction around three questions: intrinsic improvement, improvement with external information, and superiority to alternative methods. Its taxonomy checks whether initial answers receive comparable information and strong prompts, and whether correction uses unavailable oracle feedback.
papers.evaluation: The TACL article critically compares published protocols and prompt examples, with separate checklists for positive and negative findings. It identifies reliable feedback and trained correction as promising conditions, recognizes decomposable-task exceptions, and recommends direct feedback-quality measurement and compute-matched baselines.
papers.limitations: This is a qualitative review of the 2024 literature, not a new pooled experiment or exhaustive search protocol. Its negative conclusions are conditional on reviewed models, prompts and task properties. The best-initial-answer criterion requires judgment; inference-time correction does not itself demonstrate persistent learning or impossibility for later models.

papers.title: MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
papers.code_note: Code availability not verified in this review.
papers.learning_signal: Conversation history, retrieved documents, memory-pressure notices and function outcomes guide a frozen model in choosing memory edits and searches.
papers.mechanism: Separates active context from archival and recall storage. Function calls page information in and out, edit working memory, and request successive inference steps; persistent records support later conversations without changing model weights.
papers.evaluation: Augmented Multi-Session Chat tests recall and persona-based opening messages; document QA uses 50 NaturalQuestions questions, and synthetic nested-key retrieval varies nesting with 30 orderings. GPT-4-based memory retrieval improves over summary-only chat baselines; function-calling ability affects results.
papers.limitations: Chat baselines see lossy summaries while MemGPT can search full history, with different answer instructions. The recall judge is permissive; engagement is measured by similarity, not demonstrated user satisfaction. Limited benchmark horizons and premature search stopping do not establish reliable unlimited memory or reusable procedural learning.
